# vocab.design

> All 1,124 terms in the dictionary, with their definitions, under the category
> each is filed in. Every link is to the term as raw markdown; the same term is an
> HTML page at https://vocab.design/{slug}. Content is CC BY 4.0.

What the categories and tags mean, and what other kinds of page there are, is in
[llms.txt](https://vocab.design/llms.txt). Aliases, relations and implementations are
in [terms.json](https://vocab.design/terms.json).

## component

- [Accordion](https://vocab.design/accordion.md): A stack of headers, each expanding to reveal its own section of content.
- [Action list](https://vocab.design/action-list.md): A vertical list of commands with icons, descriptions and dividers, the shared body used inside menus, panels and side sheets.
- [Action sheet](https://vocab.design/action-sheet.md): A modal list of choices that slides up from the bottom of a phone screen in response to something you just did, with cancel at the end.
- [Agenda view](https://vocab.design/agenda-view.md): The same events as a chronological list grouped by day, so the next thing is at the top instead of somewhere inside a grid.
- [Alert dialog](https://vocab.design/alert-dialog.md): A dialog that interrupts the flow to demand acknowledgement or confirmation of a consequential action before anything else can continue.
- [App bar](https://vocab.design/app-bar.md): The persistent bar across the top of an application carrying its title, navigation, and primary actions.
- [App shortcut](https://vocab.design/app-shortcut.md): A short menu of app actions hung off the app icon itself, opened by a long press or a secondary click before the app is even running.
- [Attribute editor](https://vocab.design/attribute-editor.md): A repeating row of key and value fields with add and remove controls, used for tags, headers and other open ended pairs.
- [Avatar](https://vocab.design/avatar.md): A small image standing in for a person or entity, falling back to initials or a generic glyph when there is no picture.
- [Avatar group](https://vocab.design/avatar-group.md): Several avatars overlapped in a row to show a set of people compactly, with a plus n counter standing for the rest.
- [Axis](https://vocab.design/axis.md): The ruled edge of a chart that maps position to value: scale, ticks, and labels that make the marks readable as numbers.
- [Badge](https://vocab.design/badge.md): A small marker attached to another element that carries a count or a status and is not interactive on its own.
- [Banner](https://vocab.design/banner.md): A prominent message strip, usually spanning the top of a page or section, that stays visible until the user dismisses or resolves it.
- [Blame view](https://vocab.design/blame-view.md): Each line of a file labelled with the change that last touched it, so the file answers who and when rather than what it says.
- [Bottom navigation](https://vocab.design/bottom-navigation.md): A bar of three to five top level destinations pinned to the bottom edge of a phone screen, with the current destination always marked.
- [Bottom sheet](https://vocab.design/bottom-sheet.md): A surface anchored to the bottom edge that slides up over the content, often draggable between a peeked and an expanded height.
- [Breadcrumbs](https://vocab.design/breadcrumbs.md): A trail of links showing the path from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, with every level above it clickable on the way back up.
- [Bubble toolbar](https://vocab.design/bubble-toolbar.md): A small formatting bar that appears floating over a text selection and disappears when the selection is dropped.
- [Button](https://vocab.design/button.md): A control that runs an action when activated, labelled with the thing it does rather than with where it goes.
- [Button group](https://vocab.design/button-group.md): Buttons set flush against each other so they read as one unit of related actions, usually with shared borders and rounded outer corners only.
- [Calendar](https://vocab.design/calendar.md): A month grid of dates that can be read, navigated and selected from, whether standing alone or living inside a date field.
- [Callout](https://vocab.design/callout.md): A boxed note set into the flow of content to carry a warning, tip or aside, coloured by severity and staying put once shown.
- [CAPTCHA](https://vocab.design/captcha.md): A challenge placed in a form to sort people from scripts, from distorted text to a single checkbox that watches how you got there.
- [Card](https://vocab.design/card.md): A bounded surface holding a preview of one thing, usually an image, a title, some detail and one or two actions, that as a whole leads somewhere.
- [Carousel](https://vocab.design/carousel.md): A row of items shown a few at a time that advances by arrows, swipe or a timer, with the rest waiting off screen.
- [Cascader](https://vocab.design/cascader.md): A select whose options open level by level, each choice narrowing the next, used for country then state then city style data.
- [Character counter](https://vocab.design/character-counter.md): The running count beside a text box showing how many characters are used, or how many remain, against a limit.
- [Chart](https://vocab.design/chart.md): A drawing of data in which position, length, angle or colour carries the numbers, chosen so the comparison a reader needs is the easiest one to see.
- [Chart annotation](https://vocab.design/chart-annotation.md): A note pinned onto the data itself: a callout, arrow, or highlighted span that tells the reader what to see in the chart.
- [Chart legend](https://vocab.design/chart-legend.md): The key beside a chart that decodes series colours and symbols into names, and the first thing direct labeling tries to delete.
- [Chat bubble](https://vocab.design/chat-bubble.md): A rounded container for one message in a conversation, aligned and coloured by who sent it, often with a tail toward the sender's side.
- [Checkbox](https://vocab.design/checkbox.md): A square control that turns one independent option on or off, used in sets where any number of the options may be chosen.
- [Chevron](https://vocab.design/chevron.md): The small angle bracket used as a directional marker: down means this opens, right means this goes deeper, in breadcrumbs it means next level.
- [Chip](https://vocab.design/chip.md): A compact, rounded element holding one value, which can usually be selected, removed, or both.
- [Close button](https://vocab.design/close-button.md): The small dismiss control in the corner of a dialog, banner or panel, drawn as an X and named Close rather than X.
- [Coach mark](https://vocab.design/coach-mark.md): A temporary message anchored to a control that teaches what it does, often chained into a numbered sequence across a screen.
- [Code editor](https://vocab.design/code-editor.md): A text area specialised for code, with a gutter of line numbers, syntax colouring and a caret that understands indentation.
- [Color picker](https://vocab.design/color-picker.md): A control for choosing a colour, usually pairing a saturation and lightness field with a hue slider, an alpha slider and a text field for a value.
- [Color well](https://vocab.design/color-well.md): The small filled square that shows the current colour and opens a colour picker when pressed.
- [Column resizer](https://vocab.design/column-resizer.md): The invisible strip on a column border that widens or narrows the column when dragged, and often fits the column to its content on double click.
- [Combobox](https://vocab.design/combobox.md): A text input paired with a list of suggestions that narrows as you type, where the list can be navigated and chosen from with the keyboard.
- [Command palette](https://vocab.design/command-palette.md): A keyboard-summoned overlay whose single search box finds and runs any command or destination in an application by name.
- [Comparison table](https://vocab.design/comparison-table.md): A table whose columns are options and whose rows are features, read across to decide between plans or products.
- [Complication](https://vocab.design/complication.md): A slot on a watch face filled with one live figure from an app, sized to be read in the second a wrist is raised.
- [Confirmation dialog](https://vocab.design/confirmation-dialog.md): A modal that stops an action part way through to ask whether you meant it, naming the consequence in its confirm button rather than saying OK.
- [Contribution graph](https://vocab.design/contribution-graph.md): A year of days as a grid of week columns, each cell shaded by how much happened that day, so a habit reads as a pattern instead of a number.
- [Copy button](https://vocab.design/copy-button.md): A small control beside a value that copies it to the clipboard and confirms by turning into a tick for a second or two.
- [Data grid](https://vocab.design/data-grid.md): A spreadsheet-like table where individual cells take focus and can be edited, navigated cell by cell with the arrow keys.
- [Data table](https://vocab.design/data-table.md): A table built for working with data rather than reading it: sortable columns, selectable rows, and controls that act on the rows you select.
- [Date picker](https://vocab.design/date-picker.md): A field that opens a small calendar so a date can be chosen by looking at the month rather than typing it.
- [Date range picker](https://vocab.design/date-range-picker.md): A calendar that takes a start and an end date in one pass, highlighting the span between them as you move.
- [Description list](https://vocab.design/description-list.md): Paired labels and values laid out as a list of facts about one thing, rather than as a table of many things.
- [Diff viewer](https://vocab.design/diff-viewer.md): The view that puts two versions of a text against each other, side by side or interleaved, marking every line added, removed or changed and aligning what did not.
- [Disclosure](https://vocab.design/disclosure.md): A single button that shows and hides one region of content, reporting its state through aria-expanded.
- [Disclosure triangle](https://vocab.design/disclosure-triangle.md): The small triangle beside a tree item that points right when collapsed and down when open, rotating as it toggles.
- [Divider](https://vocab.design/divider.md): A thin line separating groups of content, decorative when the grouping is already clear and semantic when it is the only cue.
- [Dock](https://vocab.design/dock.md): A persistent strip of application icons anchored to a screen edge, holding launchers, running apps and pinned items in one row.
- [Drag handle](https://vocab.design/drag-handle.md): The small gripped area, often drawn as rows of dots or lines, that marks where an item may be picked up and dragged.
- [Drawer](https://vocab.design/drawer.md): A panel docked to one edge of the screen that slides in over the content, holding navigation or the details of the thing you selected.
- [Dropdown](https://vocab.design/dropdown.md): The loose everyday word for any panel that opens downward from a trigger, whatever the panel holds and whatever the trigger does with it.
- [Emergency exit button](https://vocab.design/emergency-exit-button.md): A control that leaves the current page immediately for an unrelated site and tries to clear it from history, for readers who may be watched.
- [Emoji picker](https://vocab.design/emoji-picker.md): A searchable grid of emoji organised by category, with recent choices remembered and skin tone chosen once.
- [Error bar](https://vocab.design/error-bar.md): Whiskers on a mark showing the range a value could plausibly take, so a chart does not imply precision it does not have.
- [Error message](https://vocab.design/error-message.md): The line attached to a field that says what went wrong and what to do about it, announced to assistive technology the moment it appears.
- [Expandable row](https://vocab.design/expandable-row.md): A table row that opens to reveal a detail panel beneath it, keeping the row in place instead of navigating away.
- [Eyedropper](https://vocab.design/eyedropper.md): A tool that turns the cursor into a sampler so a colour can be picked from anywhere on screen, usually with a magnified preview of the pixel under it.
- [Faceted filter](https://vocab.design/faceted-filter.md): A panel of grouped checkboxes and ranges that narrows a result set, each option usually showing how many results it would leave.
- [Fieldset](https://vocab.design/fieldset.md): A group of related form controls sharing one question, with a legend that acts as the label for the whole group.
- [Figure](https://vocab.design/figure.md): An image, table or code block bound to its caption so the two travel together and can be referred to from the running text.
- [File attachment](https://vocab.design/file-attachment.md): A row or card standing in for a file, showing its type, name and size, with the one action that file supports: download, open or remove.
- [File upload](https://vocab.design/file-upload.md): A control that takes files, by opening the system picker from a button or by accepting a drop into a marked area.
- [Filmstrip](https://vocab.design/filmstrip.md): A scrollable row of thumbnails beside a larger view, where picking one changes what the large view shows.
- [Flame graph](https://vocab.design/flame-graph.md): Stacked bars where width is time spent and depth is call nesting, so the widest plateau rather than the tallest tower is the thing worth fixing.
- [Floating action button](https://vocab.design/floating-action-button.md): A round, raised button that hovers above the content in a fixed corner, carrying the one action the screen is most for.
- [Floating label](https://vocab.design/floating-label.md): A label that sits inside an empty field and rises to the field's top edge when the field takes focus or holds a value.
- [Flowchart](https://vocab.design/flowchart.md): A diagram of steps in boxes joined by arrows, read rather than operated, and now more often generated from a few lines of text than drawn by hand.
- [Form](https://vocab.design/form.md): A grouping of controls a reader fills in and submits together, carrying the labels, validation and submit affordance for the whole set.
- [Gantt chart](https://vocab.design/gantt-chart.md): One row per task with a bar along a time axis, the bar showing when the work runs and lines between bars showing what waits for what.
- [Gauge](https://vocab.design/gauge.md): A dial style readout showing one value on an arc between a minimum and a maximum, borrowed from instrument panels.
- [Ghost button](https://vocab.design/ghost-button.md): A button with no fill and often no border until you hover it, sitting at the bottom of the emphasis ladder above a plain link.
- [Grabber](https://vocab.design/grabber.md): The short rounded bar drawn at the top of a bottom sheet to say the surface can be dragged.
- [Hamburger menu](https://vocab.design/hamburger-menu.md): A button of three stacked horizontal lines that opens a site's main navigation, usually in a panel over the page.
- [Helper text](https://vocab.design/helper-text.md): The short line under a field that explains the format or constraint before anything goes wrong.
- [Hover card](https://vocab.design/hover-card.md): A rich preview panel that appears on hover over a link or an avatar, summarising what is behind it.
- [HUD panel](https://vocab.design/hud-panel.md): A small dark translucent floating window of controls that hovers over content without taking it over, common in media and creative tools.
- [Icon](https://vocab.design/icon.md): A small graphic symbol standing for an action, object or idea, read at a glance and rarely safe to ship without a label.
- [Icon button](https://vocab.design/icon-button.md): A button whose whole label is an icon, so it needs an accessible name and usually a tooltip to say what it does.
- [Identicon](https://vocab.design/identicon.md): A generated default avatar derived deterministically from an identifier, so the same account always gets the same abstract pattern without uploading anything.
- [Image](https://vocab.design/image.md): An embedded picture, sized and cropped by the layout around it, carrying the alternative text that stands in when it cannot be seen.
- [Image comparison slider](https://vocab.design/image-comparison-slider.md): Two images stacked with a draggable divider that wipes between them, used to show a before and an after in one frame.
- [Image well](https://vocab.design/image-well.md): An editable image view that shows its current picture and accepts a replacement dragged or pasted straight into it.
- [Inline edit](https://vocab.design/inline-edit.md): Text that reads as plain content until you click it, at which point it becomes an input in the same place with save and cancel.
- [Input group](https://vocab.design/input-group.md): A field welded to text, a button or a select at one or both ends, so the addon reads as part of the same control rather than as a neighbour.
- [Input mask](https://vocab.design/input-mask.md): A field that imposes a fixed shape as you type, inserting the slashes, spaces or brackets a phone number or card number needs.
- [Kebab menu](https://vocab.design/kebab-menu.md): A menu of secondary actions opened from a trigger of three vertically stacked dots, usually at the end of a row, card, or toolbar.
- [Keyboard key](https://vocab.design/kbd.md): A key drawn as a small keycap in running text or a menu, so a shortcut reads as something you press rather than something you say.
- [Keyboard shortcuts dialog](https://vocab.design/keyboard-shortcuts-dialog.md): The panel opened by pressing question mark that lists every shortcut in the application, grouped by area.
- [Knob](https://vocab.design/knob.md): A round control turned by dragging in an arc, borrowed from hardware and mostly found in audio and creative tools.
- [Lightbox](https://vocab.design/lightbox.md): An overlay that shows one image or video large over a dimmed page, with next and previous controls and a dismiss.
- [Link](https://vocab.design/link.md): A control that navigates somewhere, named for its destination, and carrying the browser affordances of a destination (open in new tab, copy address).
- [List](https://vocab.design/list.md): A vertical run of related items presented as a set, where the shared shape of every row is what tells a reader the rows belong together.
- [Listbox](https://vocab.design/listbox.md): An always visible list of options you choose from with the keyboard or pointer, without a popup or a text field.
- [Live activity](https://vocab.design/live-activity.md): A persistent, updating view of something in progress, shown in system places like a lock screen so a reader can follow it without opening the app.
- [Meatball menu](https://vocab.design/meatball-menu.md): An overflow menu whose trigger is three horizontal dots, usually sitting at the end of a row or a card.
- [Media controls](https://vocab.design/media-controls.md): The cluster of play, pause, skip, volume and fullscreen controls attached to a player, which usually hides itself while playing.
- [Mega menu](https://vocab.design/mega-menu.md): A large navigation panel that drops from a top level item and shows many links at once, grouped into columns with headings.
- [Menu bar](https://vocab.design/menu-bar.md): A permanent horizontal row of menu titles (File, Edit, View) whose menus open on click and then follow the pointer along the row.
- [Menu bar extra](https://vocab.design/menu-bar-extra.md): A small application controlled item living in the system menu bar or tray, usually an icon that opens a compact panel of status and controls.
- [Menu button](https://vocab.design/menu-button.md): A button whose only job is to open a menu, marked with aria-haspopup and usually drawn with a downward chevron.
- [Meter](https://vocab.design/meter.md): A gauge of a known quantity within a known range, such as disk used or password strength, where the level is a fact rather than a task.
- [Minimap](https://vocab.design/minimap.md): A shrunken overview of a long document or canvas beside the scrollbar, with a box showing which part is currently on screen.
- [Modal dialog](https://vocab.design/modal-dialog.md): A window that opens over the page and takes control of it, so nothing behind can be used until the dialog is answered or dismissed.
- [Model selector](https://vocab.design/model-selector.md): The control in an assistant interface that picks which model answers, usually a menu carrying a short description of each option.
- [Multi select](https://vocab.design/multi-select.md): A select that accepts several values at once, usually showing the chosen ones as removable tokens inside the field.
- [Navigation bar](https://vocab.design/navigation-bar.md): The horizontal strip of primary destinations across the top of a site, usually holding the logo, the main sections and an account control.
- [Navigation menu](https://vocab.design/navigation-menu.md): A menu of destinations rather than commands, where opening an item moves you somewhere instead of running an action.
- [Navigation rail](https://vocab.design/navigation-rail.md): A narrow vertical strip of top level destinations at the side of a screen, used at medium widths where a bottom bar is wasteful and a drawer is too heavy.
- [Node graph](https://vocab.design/node-graph.md): A canvas of boxes wired to each other by lines, where each box does one job and the wiring between them is the thing being built, rearranged by dragging.
- [Node port](https://vocab.design/node-port.md): The typed stub on a node where a wire may land, coloured or shaped by what it accepts, so a connection that would make no sense refuses to complete.
- [Notification center](https://vocab.design/notification-center.md): A panel collecting notifications that were missed or kept, usually opened from a bell with an unread count.
- [Ornament](https://vocab.design/ornament.md): A small panel of controls that floats just outside a window edge in visionOS, staying with the window without covering its contents.
- [Overflow menu](https://vocab.design/overflow-menu.md): A menu holding the actions that do not fit in the visible interface, opened from one compact trigger.
- [Page indicator](https://vocab.design/page-indicator.md): The row of small dots under a carousel or onboarding screen showing how many pages there are and which one you are on.
- [Pagination](https://vocab.design/pagination.md): The numbered row of page links under a long result set, with previous and next controls and usually an ellipsis where numbers are skipped.
- [Password reveal toggle](https://vocab.design/password-reveal-toggle.md): The control inside a password field, usually an eye or the word Show, that switches the characters between masked and readable.
- [PIN input](https://vocab.design/pin-input.md): A row of single character boxes for a short code, where typing advances to the next box and pasting the whole code fills them all.
- [Playhead](https://vocab.design/playhead.md): The marker showing the current position in a timeline or track, which travels during playback and can be dragged to move it.
- [Popconfirm](https://vocab.design/popconfirm.md): A small confirmation bubble anchored to the control you just pressed, asking whether you meant it without opening a dialog over the page.
- [Popover](https://vocab.design/popover.md): A small surface anchored to the control that opened it, holding content or controls of its own, and dismissed by clicking away or pressing Escape.
- [Popover arrow](https://vocab.design/popover-arrow.md): The small triangle joining a popover or tooltip to the thing it belongs to, which flips and slides as the popover repositions.
- [Presence indicator](https://vocab.design/presence-indicator.md): The small coloured dot on an avatar reporting whether a person is available, away, busy or offline.
- [Progress bar](https://vocab.design/progress-bar.md): A filling bar reporting how far along a task is, determinate when the end is known and indeterminate when it is not.
- [Progress ring](https://vocab.design/progress-ring.md): A circular progress indicator that fills around a ring, often with the percentage in the middle.
- [Prompt input](https://vocab.design/prompt-input.md): The composer at the bottom of an assistant interface: a growing text area with attachment, model and send controls attached to it.
- [Property filter](https://vocab.design/property-filter.md): A search field that builds structured queries from tokens, letting a reader filter by named properties with operators rather than free text.
- [Push notification](https://vocab.design/push-notification.md): A system delivered message shown outside the app, on a lock screen or in a notification list, that has to earn the interruption it costs.
- [QR code](https://vocab.design/qr-code.md): A square matrix barcode rendered in the interface to hand a link or credential to a phone camera.
- [Quick settings tile](https://vocab.design/quick-settings-tile.md): A one tap button or toggle an app contributes to the system control surface, so one feature can be reached without opening the app.
- [Radial menu](https://vocab.design/radial-menu.md): A menu whose items sit around the point of invocation, so a choice is made by direction and distance rather than by reading a list.
- [Radio group](https://vocab.design/radio-group.md): A set of mutually exclusive options, each with its own label and control, exactly one of which can be chosen.
- [Range slider](https://vocab.design/range-slider.md): A slider with two handles on one track that sets a lower and an upper bound, so the selection is an interval rather than a point.
- [Rating](https://vocab.design/rating.md): A row of stars or similar marks that both shows a score and, when interactive, takes one.
- [Reaction picker](https://vocab.design/reaction-picker.md): A small row of emoji that appears on hover or long press so a message can be answered without a reply.
- [Reference line](https://vocab.design/reference-line.md): A line drawn at a meaningful value across a chart: a target, a threshold, an average, a before-and-after moment.
- [Relative timestamp](https://vocab.design/relative-timestamp.md): A time printed as a distance from now, two hours ago or in three days, updating itself and holding the exact time in its tooltip.
- [Resize handle](https://vocab.design/resize-handle.md): The small corner grip that lets you drag an element or window bigger and smaller, drawn as diagonal ridges on a textarea or window corner.
- [Ribbon](https://vocab.design/ribbon.md): A tall tabbed toolbar that replaces menus, grouping commands into labelled sections with the important ones drawn larger.
- [Rich text editor](https://vocab.design/rich-text-editor.md): An editing surface that shows formatting as it will appear rather than as markup, so what the writer sees is close to what readers get.
- [Rich text toolbar](https://vocab.design/rich-text-toolbar.md): The strip of formatting controls above or beside an editor, whose buttons report their state from wherever the caret sits.
- [Scheduler](https://vocab.design/scheduler.md): A grid of days crossed with hours where each event is a block in its own slot, so a week's free time is visible and an event is moved by dragging it.
- [Scope bar](https://vocab.design/scope-bar.md): The row of category buttons directly under a search field that narrows what the query searches, such as All, Mail, Files.
- [Scrollbar](https://vocab.design/scrollbar.md): The bar beside a scrollable region whose thumb shows both how much content there is and where in it you are.
- [Scrubber](https://vocab.design/scrubber.md): The seek control of a media player: a track showing elapsed and buffered time with a playhead you drag to move through it.
- [Search field](https://vocab.design/search-field.md): A text input specialised for queries, with a magnifier, a clear control and often suggestions that appear as you type.
- [Segmented control](https://vocab.design/segmented-control.md): A single control holding two to five mutually exclusive options side by side, with the current one shown as a filled segment.
- [Select](https://vocab.design/select.md): A closed control that shows the current choice and opens a list of options when pressed, with no typing.
- [Selection card](https://vocab.design/selection-card.md): A radio or checkbox dressed as a card, where the whole tile is the target and the control itself is small or absent.
- [Share sheet](https://vocab.design/share-sheet.md): The system panel of destinations and actions for sending the current item elsewhere, populated by whatever apps are installed.
- [Show more toggle](https://vocab.design/show-more-toggle.md): The control at the end of clamped text that expands it to full length and, when honest, collapses it again.
- [Signature pad](https://vocab.design/signature-pad.md): A drawing area that captures a handwritten signature by pointer or touch, with a clear control and a baseline to sign on.
- [Slider](https://vocab.design/slider.md): A control that sets a value by dragging a handle along a track, showing the whole range at once.
- [Sort indicator](https://vocab.design/sort-indicator.md): The small arrow in a column header showing that the table is sorted by that column and in which direction.
- [Sparkline](https://vocab.design/sparkline.md): A tiny chart with no axes or labels, drawn inline at text size to show the shape of a trend beside the number it belongs to.
- [Speed dial](https://vocab.design/speed-dial.md): A floating action button that fans out into three to six smaller related actions when pressed or hovered.
- [Spinner](https://vocab.design/spinner.md): An indeterminate loading indicator that shows work is happening without saying how much of it is left.
- [Split button](https://vocab.design/split-button.md): A two part control where the main area runs a default action and an attached arrow opens a menu of related alternatives.
- [Splitter](https://vocab.design/splitter.md): The draggable bar between two panes that changes how much room each one gets, keyboard operable as a slider between limits.
- [Stat](https://vocab.design/stat.md): A single number shown large with a label and often a change indicator, the unit a dashboard is built from.
- [Step indicator](https://vocab.design/step-indicator.md): A row or column of numbered stages showing where you are in a multi step flow and what remains.
- [Stepper](https://vocab.design/stepper.md): A small two part control with minus and plus that nudges a number up or down one step at a time.
- [Submenu](https://vocab.design/submenu.md): A menu that opens sideways from a menu item, marked by a trailing arrow, and stays open while the pointer travels diagonally toward it.
- [Switch](https://vocab.design/switch.md): A control shaped like a sliding track that turns one setting on or off and applies the change the moment it is flipped, with no separate save step.
- [Tabs](https://vocab.design/tabs.md): A set of labelled panels in one region, where selecting a label swaps the panel beneath it.
- [Tag](https://vocab.design/tag.md): A small label attached to an item to classify it, often coloured by category and sometimes removable.
- [Tag input](https://vocab.design/tag-input.md): A field that turns each entry into a removable tag sitting inside the field, with the caret waiting after the last one.
- [Tearsheet](https://vocab.design/tearsheet.md): A tall modal anchored to the bottom of the viewport that holds a multi step creation flow, stackable when one flow opens another.
- [Text area](https://vocab.design/textarea.md): A multi-line text box, usually resizable, for input that will not fit on one line: a comment, a description, an address, a note.
- [Text field](https://vocab.design/text-field.md): A single line box for typed input, carrying a label, an optional hint, and the error message shown when what was typed does not pass.
- [Three-way merge](https://vocab.design/three-way-merge.md): Three versions on screen at once, mine, theirs, and the ancestor they both came from, with the result edited underneath so a conflict is decided rather than guessed.
- [Thumbnail](https://vocab.design/thumbnail.md): A small stand-in image for a larger one, cropped rather than letterboxed so a row of them lines up.
- [Tick marks](https://vocab.design/tick-marks.md): The small notches printed along a slider track that show the discrete stops the handle can land on.
- [Time picker](https://vocab.design/time-picker.md): A control for choosing a time of day, either as a dial you tap around or as hour and minute lists.
- [Timeline](https://vocab.design/timeline.md): A vertical or horizontal line of dated events, each pinned to the line by a marker and reading in order.
- [Title bar](https://vocab.design/title-bar.md): The strip along the top of a window carrying its title and window controls, and the region you drag to move the window.
- [Toast](https://vocab.design/toast.md): A brief, self-dismissing message that appears at a screen edge to confirm an action or report status without interrupting the user's flow.
- [Toggle button](https://vocab.design/toggle-button.md): A button that stays pressed, reporting an on or off state through aria-pressed rather than firing and returning.
- [Toggle group](https://vocab.design/toggle-group.md): A set of toggle buttons treated as one control, either single select like radios or multi select like a row of formatting toggles.
- [Toggletip](https://vocab.design/toggletip.md): A tip revealed by clicking rather than hovering, so it works by touch and may contain links or controls a tooltip could not.
- [Toolbar](https://vocab.design/toolbar.md): A grouped row of controls acting on the current view, sharing one tab stop and moving focus between its items with arrow keys.
- [Tooltip](https://vocab.design/tooltip.md): A brief text label shown on hover or keyboard focus that names or explains the element it points at, and carries nothing you can interact with.
- [Trace viewer](https://vocab.design/trace-viewer.md): The view that lays a request's spans on one time axis, each nested under the span that called it, so the bar that is too long or starts too late is the finding.
- [Track](https://vocab.design/track.md): The groove a slider thumb or scrollbar travels along, usually drawn as filled before the handle and empty after it.
- [Transfer list](https://vocab.design/transfer-list.md): Two side by side lists with arrow buttons between them, used to move items from available to chosen and back.
- [Tree grid](https://vocab.design/treegrid.md): A table whose rows nest and expand like a tree, so hierarchy and columns of data coexist in one grid.
- [Tree select](https://vocab.design/tree-select.md): A select whose popup is a tree, so options can be chosen at any depth with parents collapsing over their children.
- [Tree view](https://vocab.design/treeview.md): A nested list where branches expand and collapse in place, navigated with arrow keys as a single tab stop.
- [Typing indicator](https://vocab.design/typing-indicator.md): The three bouncing dots shown while someone is composing a reply, or while an assistant is preparing one.
- [Utility bar](https://vocab.design/utility-bar.md): A persistent bar docked to the bottom of an application holding small tools that open into panels without leaving the current page.
- [Video player](https://vocab.design/video-player.md): A framed video with the controls needed to play, seek, mute and caption it, sized so the controls never crowd the picture.
- [Virtual keyboard](https://vocab.design/virtual-keyboard.md): The on screen keyboard a device raises for a field, whose key set the field itself chooses by declaring what kind of value it wants.
- [Watermark](https://vocab.design/watermark.md): Repeating faint text or a mark tiled across content to claim it or to mark it as a draft or a preview.
- [Waveform](https://vocab.design/waveform.md): An audio track drawn as a row of amplitude bars, used both to show what is in the file and as the surface you scrub along.
- [Welcome mat](https://vocab.design/welcome-mat.md): A full width introduction shown on first entry to a feature, listing what is new or what to set up, with a way to skip it for good.
- [Wheel picker](https://vocab.design/wheel-picker.md): A spinning drum of values that snaps to the item under a fixed selection line, the iOS way of choosing from a short list.
- [Widget](https://vocab.design/widget.md): A small, glanceable view of an app placed on a system surface such as a home screen or desktop, sized in fixed slots rather than freely.
- [Window controls](https://vocab.design/window-controls.md): The cluster of close, minimise and zoom controls in a window's title bar, three coloured dots on macOS and three glyphs on Windows.
- [Wizard](https://vocab.design/wizard.md): A flow broken into ordered steps with back and next controls, where each step validates before the next one is allowed.
- [Zebra striping](https://vocab.design/zebra-striping.md): Alternating row backgrounds in a table so the eye can track a single row across many columns.

## layout

- [12 column grid](https://vocab.design/twelve-column-grid.md): The web's default column count, chosen because twelve divides cleanly into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.
- [8 point grid](https://vocab.design/eight-point-grid.md): A spacing convention where every size and gap is a multiple of eight, so values stay whole numbers at every common screen density.
- [Adaptive layout](https://vocab.design/adaptive-layout.md): A layout that switches between a few discrete arrangements chosen per size class, rather than flowing continuously as the window changes.
- [Anchor positioning](https://vocab.design/anchor-positioning.md): A CSS mechanism that tethers one element to another, sizing and placing it against its anchor and trying fallback positions when the default one would overflow.
- [App shell](https://vocab.design/app-shell.md): The persistent frame of an application, its header, navigation and footer, that stays put while only the content region swaps as you move around.
- [App silhouette](https://vocab.design/app-silhouette.md): The recognisable outline of an app's chrome, which bars and panes it has and where they sit, used to classify one app's layout against another's.
- [Aspect ratio box](https://vocab.design/aspect-ratio-box.md): A container that holds a fixed width to height proportion whatever its size, so media reserves its space before it loads.
- [Baseline grid](https://vocab.design/baseline-grid.md): A set of evenly spaced horizontal lines that every line of text sits on, so type in adjacent columns lines up across the page.
- [Bento grid](https://vocab.design/bento-grid.md): A grid whose cells are deliberately different sizes, tiled to fill a rectangle without gaps, like the compartments of a bento box.
- [Box](https://vocab.design/box.md): A bordered container, optionally titled, that groups logically related controls so the grouping is drawn rather than implied by spacing alone.
- [Breakout](https://vocab.design/breakout.md): A track wider than the reading column but narrower than the viewport, used for figures and code that need more room than prose.
- [Breakpoint](https://vocab.design/breakpoint.md): A viewport width at which a layout is allowed to change shape, defined once so every screen in a system reflows at the same places.
- [Broken grid](https://vocab.design/broken-grid.md): A composition that sets up a grid and then deliberately violates it, overlapping and offsetting elements to create tension.
- [Bypassing pattern](https://vocab.design/bypassing-pattern.md): A scanning shape where readers deliberately skip the opening words of each line because every line in a list starts the same way.
- [Canonical layout](https://vocab.design/canonical-layout.md): One of a small set of proven multi pane arrangements a platform recommends, such as list detail, supporting pane and feed, instead of a new layout per screen.
- [Card grid](https://vocab.design/card-grid.md): Content laid out as equal width cards flowing across a responsive grid and wrapping to new rows as space allows.
- [Chart aspect ratio](https://vocab.design/chart-aspect-ratio.md): How wide a chart is for its height, which sets the slopes of its lines; banking to 45 degrees keeps rates of change readable.
- [Chrome](https://vocab.design/chrome.md): The parts of a window or app that frame content rather than being content: title bars, toolbars, tab strips and address bars.
- [Cluster](https://vocab.design/cluster.md): A layout primitive that lays items of differing widths out like words in a paragraph, wrapping to new lines with even gaps in both directions.
- [Column drop](https://vocab.design/column-drop.md): A responsive pattern where full height columns peel off one at a time and stack below as the viewport narrows, keeping source order.
- [Column offset](https://vocab.design/column-offset.md): Pushing a column away from the grid's start so it begins on a later line, leaving deliberate empty tracks rather than an element to fill them.
- [Commitment pattern](https://vocab.design/commitment-pattern.md): The rare scanning shape where a motivated reader fixates on nearly every word, the only pattern that behaves like actual reading.
- [Common region](https://vocab.design/common-region.md): The grouping principle that anything inside a shared boundary reads as one group, strong enough to beat how far apart the items actually are.
- [Compound grid](https://vocab.design/compound-grid.md): Two or more grids of different column counts overlaid in one layout, so a page can carry several rhythms while still sharing one structure.
- [Container](https://vocab.design/container.md): A wrapper that caps how wide content can get and adds the side padding that keeps it off the viewport edges.
- [Container query](https://vocab.design/container-query.md): A rule that responds to the size of a component's own container rather than the viewport, so one component adapts anywhere it is placed.
- [Containing block](https://vocab.design/containing-block.md): The box an element's percentages and offsets are measured against, which is not always its parent and changes with how the element is positioned.
- [Content choreography](https://vocab.design/content-choreography.md): Deciding how blocks of content reorder and regroup as a layout reflows, so hierarchy survives the collapse from several columns into one.
- [Content shelf](https://vocab.design/content-shelf.md): A horizontally scrolling row of cards, one row per category, stacked down the page so each row is browsed sideways.
- [Cover](https://vocab.design/cover.md): A layout primitive that fills at least the viewport height, centring a principal element vertically with optional header and footer pinned above and below.
- [Dashboard grid](https://vocab.design/dashboard-grid.md): A grid of tiles, each holding one metric, chart or list, that a reader can often resize and rearrange.
- [Deconstructed pancake](https://vocab.design/deconstructed-pancake.md): A row of equal cards that wraps to fewer per line as space runs out, with the last line left aligned at its natural size rather than stretched to fill.
- [Density](https://vocab.design/density.md): How much content a system packs into a given area, tuned as a named setting so the same components can run comfortable or compact.
- [Density independent pixel](https://vocab.design/density-independent-pixel.md): A virtual unit of length that stays the same physical size across screen densities, so one number can describe a layout on every device.
- [Device posture](https://vocab.design/device-posture.md): The physical fold state of a foldable device, such as flat, book or tabletop, which a layout can respond to alongside plain size.
- [Display cutout](https://vocab.design/display-cutout.md): The camera housing that intrudes into the screen rectangle, which a layout has to route content around rather than under.
- [Edge routing](https://vocab.design/edge-routing.md): How a connector gets from one node to another: a bezier sweep, a right-angled staircase, or a straight line, picked so the crossings stay readable.
- [Edge to edge](https://vocab.design/edge-to-edge.md): Drawing an app behind the system bars so content reaches the physical screen edges, with insets applied only to what must stay tappable.
- [F pattern](https://vocab.design/f-pattern.md): The scanning shape eye tracking finds on text heavy pages: two horizontal sweeps across the top, then a vertical run down the left edge.
- [Feed layout](https://vocab.design/feed-layout.md): A scrolling column or adaptive grid of equivalent items built for browsing, where no item outranks another by position alone.
- [Fisheye view](https://vocab.design/fisheye-view.md): A focus plus context display that magnifies whatever has attention and progressively compresses everything further away, like a lens dragged along a list.
- [Fluid grid](https://vocab.design/fluid-grid.md): A grid whose columns and gutters are expressed as proportions rather than fixed pixels, so the whole composition stretches and shrinks with its container.
- [Fluid hybrid](https://vocab.design/fluid-hybrid.md): A mail layout that reflows with no media query at all: percentage widths held in by max-width, with fixed-width ghost tables that only Outlook can see.
- [Fluid space scale](https://vocab.design/fluid-space-scale.md): A spacing ramp whose every step interpolates between a minimum and a maximum viewport, so gaps grow smoothly with the screen instead of jumping at breakpoints.
- [Focal point](https://vocab.design/focal-point.md): The one element a composition is built around, given enough size, contrast or isolation that the eye lands there before anywhere else.
- [Focus plus context](https://vocab.design/focus-plus-context.md): A layout that keeps one region in full detail inside its own surroundings, shrinking or dimming the context instead of moving it into a second pane.
- [Frozen column](https://vocab.design/frozen-column.md): A table column held against the edge while the rest scrolls sideways, so the row's identifying value stays readable.
- [Full bleed](https://vocab.design/full-bleed.md): An element that breaks past the content column to span the whole viewport width while its neighbours stay constrained.
- [Global navigation](https://vocab.design/global-navigation.md): The links to the top tier of a site's structure, present on every page and unchanged wherever the reader currently is.
- [Golden ratio](https://vocab.design/golden-ratio.md): The proportion of roughly 1 to 1.618 used to divide a layout, so its parts relate to each other by a rule instead of by arbitrary numbers.
- [Graph layout](https://vocab.design/graph-layout.md): Placing the nodes of a wired diagram by algorithm rather than by hand: layered for a flow, radial for a hub, force-directed for a mesh that has no direction.
- [Grid lanes](https://vocab.design/grid-lanes.md): The native masonry mechanism in CSS grid, where one axis keeps strict tracks and the other lets items stack into whichever lane has room.
- [Gutenberg diagram](https://vocab.design/gutenberg-diagram.md): A model splitting evenly weighted pages into four quadrants, with the eye falling from the primary area at top left to the terminal area at bottom right.
- [Gutter](https://vocab.design/gutter.md): The space between columns or tracks in a grid, distinct from the outer margin that separates the grid from the container edge.
- [Hero](https://vocab.design/hero.md): The large opening block of a page carrying a headline, a supporting line, imagery, and the main call to action.
- [Holy grail layout](https://vocab.design/holy-grail-layout.md): A three column page with header and footer where the centre column is fluid, the two side columns are fixed, and all three appear equal height.
- [Home indicator](https://vocab.design/home-indicator.md): The thin bar at the bottom of a gesture driven phone screen, reserved space that app content must not sit beneath.
- [Imposter](https://vocab.design/imposter.md): A layout primitive that positions one element centred over its container, overlapping whatever is beneath rather than taking a place in the flow.
- [Infinite canvas](https://vocab.design/infinite-canvas.md): A workspace with no page edges, where content is placed anywhere in an unbounded plane and the viewport pans and zooms over it instead of scrolling a document.
- [Inspector](https://vocab.design/inspector.md): A pane, usually on the trailing edge, that shows and edits the properties of whatever is currently selected.
- [Intrinsic web design](https://vocab.design/intrinsic-web-design.md): Building layouts from what the content needs, using grid, flexbox and intrinsic sizing together, instead of imposing a fixed column skeleton.
- [Justified gallery](https://vocab.design/justified-gallery.md): A photo grid that scales and trims images so every row lands on one shared height with flush left and right edges, unlike masonry's ragged columns.
- [Kanban board](https://vocab.design/kanban-board.md): A row of vertical columns, each one a stage, holding cards that move sideways as work progresses.
- [Keyline](https://vocab.design/keyline.md): An invisible line that content across a whole screen aligns to, such as the edge line every row starts at and the deeper line where text begins after an icon.
- [Lawn mower pattern](https://vocab.design/lawn-mower-pattern.md): A scanning shape for tables where the eye runs across one row, drops down and runs back the other way, mowing the cells in alternating directions.
- [Layer cake pattern](https://vocab.design/layer-cake-pattern.md): A scanning shape where the eye reads headings and subheadings and skips the text between them, so the fixation map looks like stacked layers.
- [Layout grid](https://vocab.design/layout-grid.md): The shared column, gutter and margin structure a team lays every screen against, so different people's pages line up with each other.
- [Layout margins](https://vocab.design/layout-margins.md): The reserved space between a container's edge and its content, sized by the system so content never touches the edge of the screen.
- [Layout shift](https://vocab.design/layout-shift.md): Content moving after it has already been painted, usually because something arriving late took space that was never reserved for it.
- [Layout shifter](https://vocab.design/layout-shifter.md): A responsive pattern where the arrangement genuinely differs per breakpoint rather than reflowing, so each size gets its own composition.
- [Letterboxing](https://vocab.design/letterboxing.md): Filling the mismatch between content shape and frame shape with bars: above and below for letterbox, at the sides for pillarbox.
- [List detail](https://vocab.design/list-detail.md): A browsable list paired with a pane showing the selected item in full, collapsing to one screen at a time when the window is narrow.
- [Local navigation](https://vocab.design/local-navigation.md): Links contextual to where the reader is, showing the siblings and children of the current page rather than the whole site.
- [Logical properties](https://vocab.design/logical-properties.md): Layout properties named by flow direction (inline start, block end) rather than by screen edge, so a layout mirrors itself in other writing modes.
- [Logo cloud](https://vocab.design/logo-cloud.md): A row or grid of customer logos used as social proof, usually flattened to one colour so no brand dominates.
- [Magazine layout](https://vocab.design/magazine-layout.md): An editorial composition with mixed column widths, one dominant lead story and smaller supporting items arranged around it.
- [Marking pattern](https://vocab.design/marking-pattern.md): A scanning shape where the eye holds one spot on the screen while content scrolls past underneath it, most common on phones.
- [Masonry](https://vocab.design/masonry.md): A column layout that packs items of unequal height by placing each one in the shortest column, so the rows never line up and the bottom edge stays ragged.
- [Media object](https://vocab.design/media-object.md): The pairing of a fixed size image or avatar on one side with a heading and text that fills the rest, repeated everywhere in interfaces.
- [Miller columns](https://vocab.design/miller-columns.md): A browsing layout of side-by-side columns where selecting an item in one column fills the next with its children, keeping the whole path visible.
- [Mobile first](https://vocab.design/mobile-first.md): Designing and writing the narrow layout first and adding rules as space is gained, so the small screen is the default rather than the fallback.
- [Modular grid](https://vocab.design/modular-grid.md): A grid with both columns and rows, dividing the page into equal modules that content can span in either direction.
- [Mostly fluid](https://vocab.design/mostly-fluid.md): A responsive pattern where a multi column grid stretches with the viewport up to a maximum width, then centres, stacking only on the smallest screens.
- [Multi column layout](https://vocab.design/multi-column-layout.md): An application shell with three or more vertical regions, typically navigation, a list, and a reading pane, as in a mail client.
- [Multi-window mode](https://vocab.design/multi-window-mode.md): A windowing mode where two or more apps share one screen, side by side, stacked, or as freeform windows, so every app must survive being any size.
- [Named grid areas](https://vocab.design/named-grid-areas.md): Naming regions of a grid and drawing the layout as rows of those names, so items are placed by name instead of by line number.
- [Object fit](https://vocab.design/object-fit.md): How a picture or video is resized inside a box whose shape it does not match: stretched to fill, letterboxed to fit whole, or cropped to cover every edge.
- [Off canvas](https://vocab.design/off-canvas.md): Keeping secondary regions parked outside the viewport and sliding them in on demand, instead of stacking them below the main content.
- [Optical alignment](https://vocab.design/optical-alignment.md): Nudging an element off its measured position so it looks aligned, correcting for shapes whose bounding box lies about their visual centre.
- [Overscan safe area](https://vocab.design/overscan-safe-area.md): The inset a television layout keeps clear of the screen edge, about five percent, because sets crop the outer frame and anything near it disappears.
- [Overview plus detail](https://vocab.design/overview-plus-detail.md): A layout that shows a compressed overview and a detailed view at the same time in separate regions, so the reader keeps their place while inspecting one part.
- [Page break](https://vocab.design/page-break.md): Where content is cut to continue in the next fragment, a printed page, a column or a region, plus the rules that decide where the cut may fall.
- [Page header](https://vocab.design/page-header.md): The band at the top of a screen carrying the page title, its context, and the actions that apply to the page as a whole.
- [Pancake stack](https://vocab.design/pancake-stack.md): A three row page where the header and footer take only the height they need and the middle row absorbs every remaining pixel, even when the content is short.
- [Pane](https://vocab.design/pane.md): A layout container that holds one destination's content inside a window, either fixed or flexible in width, combined with other panes to fill the space.
- [Picture in picture](https://vocab.design/picture-in-picture.md): A small always on top window that keeps video or navigation visible in a corner while the reader works in another app or scrolls another page.
- [Pixel density](https://vocab.design/pixel-density.md): How many physical pixels a display packs into an inch, and the reason a CSS pixel is a unit of measure rather than a dot on the screen.
- [Proximity](https://vocab.design/proximity.md): The grouping principle that elements placed close together read as related, which is why spacing decides perceived structure more reliably than borders do.
- [RAM technique](https://vocab.design/ram-technique.md): A grid that decides its own column count from a minimum item width, so the same one line rule works at every screen size without a single breakpoint.
- [Responsive upscaling](https://vocab.design/responsive-upscaling.md): Designing what a layout does with the space it gains on very wide screens, rather than only what it drops as screens narrow.
- [Responsive web design](https://vocab.design/responsive-web-design.md): One layout that adapts to any screen through fluid grids, flexible images and media queries, rather than a separate site built for each class of device.
- [RTL mirroring](https://vocab.design/rtl-mirroring.md): Flipping a layout horizontally for right to left languages, moving navigation and progression to the other side while leaving some elements unmirrored.
- [Rule of thirds](https://vocab.design/rule-of-thirds.md): Dividing a frame into nine equal cells with two lines each way and placing the important elements on the lines or their intersections.
- [Safe area](https://vocab.design/safe-area.md): The part of the screen guaranteed clear of notches, system bars and rounded corners, where interactive content can safely sit.
- [Scaffold](https://vocab.design/scaffold.md): The frame that positions an app's persistent regions, its bars, panes and body, so each screen drops content into named slots instead of inventing its own arrangement.
- [Scroll container](https://vocab.design/scroll-container.md): The element that actually scrolls its overflowing content, distinct from the page, and the box the browser calls the scrollport.
- [Scroll snap](https://vocab.design/scroll-snap.md): Snap positions declared on a scroll container so scrolling settles on a chosen item edge instead of stopping wherever momentum runs out.
- [Semantic zoom](https://vocab.design/semantic-zoom.md): Switching between two views of the same content, a zoomed out view of group headings and a zoomed in view of individual items, instead of scaling pixels.
- [Sidebar](https://vocab.design/sidebar.md): A persistent vertical region alongside the main content holding navigation or secondary controls, often collapsible on narrow screens.
- [Sidenote](https://vocab.design/sidenote.md): A note placed in the outer margin beside the line it belongs to, rather than collected at the foot of the page.
- [Site footer](https://vocab.design/site-footer.md): The closing region of a site holding secondary navigation, legal links, and contact details that do not deserve top level placement.
- [Small multiples](https://vocab.design/small-multiples.md): The same small chart repeated in a grid, once per category, so comparison happens by eye movement instead of overplotting.
- [Spacer](https://vocab.design/spacer.md): A deliberate empty element between regions: the gap between two panes that carries the drag handle when they resize, or the flexible filler that pushes toolbar items apart.
- [Spacing scale](https://vocab.design/spacing-scale.md): The fixed, named set of spacing values a system allows, so gaps come from a shortlist instead of being invented per screen.
- [Spanned layout](https://vocab.design/spanned-layout.md): How an app arranges itself when one window is stretched across two displays, either keeping content clear of the seam or splitting the layout exactly at it.
- [Split screen layout](https://vocab.design/split-screen-layout.md): A page cut into two equal full height halves, each carrying its own message or path, with no hierarchy between them.
- [Split view](https://vocab.design/split-view.md): A layout of two or more side by side panes where a choice in the leading pane decides what the trailing pane shows.
- [Spotted pattern](https://vocab.design/spotted-pattern.md): A scanning shape where the eye jumps to isolated words scattered down the page, hunting a keyword, a link or a number rather than reading anything.
- [Stack](https://vocab.design/stack.md): A layout primitive that puts one consistent gap between every child in a vertical run, so spacing lives with the parent instead of each item.
- [Stacking context](https://vocab.design/stacking-context.md): A self contained depth ordering created by certain properties, inside which z-index only competes locally and can never escape to the level above.
- [Status bar](https://vocab.design/status-bar.md): A thin strip along the edge of a window or screen that reports state and offers only minor actions, never the primary ones.
- [Sticky footer](https://vocab.design/sticky-footer.md): A footer held against the bottom of the viewport when the page is short, and pushed below the content when the page is long.
- [Sticky header](https://vocab.design/sticky-header.md): A header that scrolls away with the page until it reaches the top edge, then stays fixed there while the rest keeps moving.
- [Sticky sidebar](https://vocab.design/sticky-sidebar.md): A side column that scrolls with the page and then holds in place once its top reaches the viewport edge, releasing at the end of its container.
- [Subgrid](https://vocab.design/subgrid.md): A nested grid that borrows its parent's tracks instead of defining its own, so contents of separate children still line up with each other.
- [Supporting pane](https://vocab.design/supporting-pane.md): A secondary pane holding content that only makes sense next to the main pane, placed beside it on wide windows and below it or behind a control on narrow ones.
- [Switcher](https://vocab.design/switcher.md): A layout primitive that flips between a row and a column at a threshold it works out from its own width, with no media query involved.
- [Table-based layout](https://vocab.design/table-based-layout.md): Laying a page out in nested tables because the renderer has no box model worth trusting, which is how mail is still built and how the web was built before CSS.
- [Text columns](https://vocab.design/text-columns.md): Flowing one block of running text into several columns that fill and balance automatically, with an optional rule drawn between them.
- [The fold](https://vocab.design/the-fold.md): The bottom edge of the first screenful, above which content is seen without any scrolling and below which it must be earned.
- [Thumb zone](https://vocab.design/thumb-zone.md): The arc of a phone screen a thumb reaches comfortably in a one handed grip, with harder to reach bands above and across from it.
- [Tiny tweaks](https://vocab.design/tiny-tweaks.md): The lightest responsive pattern: a single column design that only adjusts type size, image size and margins as the screen changes.
- [Top layer](https://vocab.design/top-layer.md): The layer above everything else in a document where fullscreen elements, modal dialogs and popovers render, escaping every ancestor's clipping and stacking order.
- [Top shelf](https://vocab.design/top-shelf.md): The band across the top of a television home screen that the focused app fills with its own content, so an app advertises itself before anyone opens it.
- [Universal navigation](https://vocab.design/universal-navigation.md): A slim bar that links a subsite back to its parent organisation's other sites, sitting above the subsite's own global navigation.
- [Utility navigation](https://vocab.design/utility-navigation.md): The strip of secondary tools and account actions, sign in, search, language, cart, kept apart from the links that describe the site's content.
- [Viewport](https://vocab.design/viewport.md): The visible rectangle of a page inside the browser window, excluding the browser's own bars, and the unit basis for vh and vw.
- [Visual balance](https://vocab.design/visual-balance.md): The distribution of visual weight across a composition, reached by mirroring elements, by setting one large element against several small ones, or by radiating from a centre.
- [Visual hierarchy](https://vocab.design/visual-hierarchy.md): The ordering of elements by visual weight, size, contrast, position and spacing, so a reader learns what matters most without being told.
- [Whitespace](https://vocab.design/whitespace.md): The empty area between and around elements, treated as an active design material rather than as leftover space.
- [Window size class](https://vocab.design/window-size-class.md): A named bucket for how much width an app window has, such as compact, medium and expanded, used in place of raw device categories.
- [Z pattern](https://vocab.design/z-pattern.md): The scanning shape on sparse pages: across the top, diagonally down to the lower left, then across the bottom to the final call to action.
- [Zigzag layout](https://vocab.design/zigzag-layout.md): Alternating rows that flip which side the image and the text sit on, so the eye zigzags down a list of features.

## pattern

- [10-foot UI](https://vocab.design/ten-foot-ui.md): The register for screens read from a couch: focus-driven navigation with a remote, oversized type and cards, horizontal rails, and safe margins for TV overscan.
- [Achievement badge](https://vocab.design/achievement-badge.md): A collectible marker awarded for a milestone and displayed on a profile, often shown greyed out before it is earned so the set is visible.
- [Activity feed](https://vocab.design/activity-feed.md): A reverse chronological list of things that happened, each entry naming an actor, a verb, and an object, grouped when many are alike.
- [Address autocomplete](https://vocab.design/address-autocomplete.md): Replacing a set of address fields with one lookup that suggests full addresses after a few characters and fills the rest on selection.
- [Anti-pattern](https://vocab.design/anti-pattern.md): A solution reached for again and again for a familiar problem, which fails at the thing it was reached for and often leaves the situation worse than doing nothing.
- [Applied filters](https://vocab.design/applied-filters.md): A row of removable tokens above the results showing every filter currently in force, with a control to clear them all at once.
- [Autofill](https://vocab.design/autofill.md): The browser filling a form from values it has already saved, on its own or from a dropdown of the reader's own profile, so a field arrives answered.
- [Autoplay](https://vocab.design/autoplay.md): Playback that starts with no gesture from the reader, which browsers now allow only while the sound is off, so autoplay in practice means a silent moving picture.
- [Autosave](https://vocab.design/autosave.md): Persisting the reader's work continuously without a save action, usually with a quiet status line reporting when the last save happened.
- [Back to top](https://vocab.design/back-to-top.md): A control that appears after the reader has scrolled some distance and returns them to the top of the page in one action.
- [Bulk actions](https://vocab.design/bulk-actions.md): Selecting several rows and applying one command to all of them, usually through a bar that appears once a selection exists and reports its count.
- [Bulletproof button](https://vocab.design/bulletproof-button.md): A mail button built to survive a renderer that drops CSS: the fill carried by a cell or box behind the link rather than by a background the client can refuse.
- [Chartjunk](https://vocab.design/chartjunk.md): Tufte's word for ink that decorates a chart without carrying data: 3D bevels, gradient fills, mascots, gridline thickets.
- [Check answers](https://vocab.design/check-answers.md): A review screen listing everything the reader entered, with a change link beside each answer, shown before the submission is final.
- [Comparison prevention](https://vocab.design/comparison-prevention.md): Structuring plans or products so their features and prices cannot be lined up, forcing a decision that no side-by-side reading would support.
- [Confirmation page](https://vocab.design/confirmation-page.md): The screen that closes a transaction, stating plainly that it succeeded, giving a reference the reader can quote, and saying what happens next.
- [Confirmshaming](https://vocab.design/confirmshaming.md): Wording the decline option so that choosing it is an admission of something embarrassing, making refusal feel like a confession rather than a choice.
- [Conversational interface](https://vocab.design/conversational-interface.md): An interface operated in turns of language rather than by controls, where the transcript is the state and the only visible affordance is a box to type in.
- [Cookie consent banner](https://vocab.design/cookie-consent-banner.md): A notice asking permission to store non-essential cookies before the reader has done anything, offering accept, reject, and a route to per-purpose choices.
- [Countdown timer](https://vocab.design/countdown-timer.md): A running clock attached to an offer or a held resource, showing how long remains and what will happen when it reaches zero.
- [Cursor pagination](https://vocab.design/cursor-pagination.md): Paging that moves by a pointer into the result set rather than a page number, so newly inserted rows never shift what the next page contains.
- [Dark mode email](https://vocab.design/dark-mode-email.md): Designing a mail for clients that will invert its palette without asking, where a near-black behaves better than black and a logo needs a ground it survives on.
- [Dark pattern](https://vocab.design/dark-pattern.md): An interface arranged to make the reader do something they did not intend and would not have chosen, by exploiting how attention and defaults work.
- [Data-ink ratio](https://vocab.design/data-ink-ratio.md): Tufte's measure of chart economy: the share of ink that would be missed if erased, with everything else a candidate for deletion.
- [Did you mean](https://vocab.design/did-you-mean.md): Offering a corrected spelling for a query that returned little or nothing, either as a suggestion to accept or as a substitution the reader can undo.
- [Diegetic interface](https://vocab.design/diegetic-interface.md): An interface that exists inside the fiction it serves, so the character can see and use it too, rather than being drawn on top of the world for the player alone.
- [Direct labeling](https://vocab.design/direct-labeling.md): Writing series names next to the data instead of in a legend, trading a lookup for a glance.
- [Direct manipulation](https://vocab.design/direct-manipulation.md): Acting on an object by handling the object itself, dragging, resizing, or typing into it, rather than describing the change in a separate control.
- [Disguised ad](https://vocab.design/disguised-ad.md): An advertisement styled to look like a control or an item of content, so the click it collects was aimed at something else entirely.
- [Double opt-in](https://vocab.design/double-opt-in.md): Asking a new subscriber to confirm from the address they typed, so a list holds only addresses whose owner agreed and a typo never becomes a stranger's mail.
- [Drag preview](https://vocab.design/drag-preview.md): The semi-transparent copy of the dragged item that follows the pointer, sometimes collapsed into a stack when several items move at once.
- [Drag to reorder](https://vocab.design/drag-to-reorder.md): Changing the order of a list by dragging an item to a new position, with the remaining items shifting to show where it will land.
- [Drill-down navigation](https://vocab.design/drill-down-navigation.md): Going deeper into a hierarchy one level at a time inside the same panel, each level replacing the last and offering a way back up.
- [Drip pricing](https://vocab.design/drip-pricing.md): Advertising a low headline price and adding mandatory fees one screen at a time, so the true total only appears once the buyer is committed.
- [Drop indicator](https://vocab.design/drop-indicator.md): The line or highlighted gap drawn during a drag to show exactly where the item will land if it is released now.
- [Dual axis](https://vocab.design/dual-axis.md): Two value axes sharing one plot so two series can be compared, and a free knob for manufacturing whatever correlation you like.
- [Empty state](https://vocab.design/empty-state.md): The screen a container shows when it holds nothing, naming the absence and offering the action that ends it.
- [Endowed progress](https://vocab.design/endowed-progress.md): Starting a progress meter part filled, so the reader feels they are continuing something already begun rather than starting from nothing.
- [Error page](https://vocab.design/error-page.md): The whole screen a site serves instead of the page that was asked for: what happened, in the reader's words, and the shortest way back to something that works.
- [Error summary](https://vocab.design/error-summary.md): A block at the top of a failed form listing every problem as links that move focus to the field that caused it.
- [Express checkout](https://vocab.design/express-checkout.md): A row of one-tap payment buttons placed above the normal form, which fetch address and payment details from a wallet the buyer already has.
- [Faceted search](https://vocab.design/faceted-search.md): Narrowing results by ticking values from several independent attribute groups, with counts showing how many results each value would leave.
- [Fake door](https://vocab.design/fake-door.md): A control that looks shipped and leads nowhere, put in the interface on purpose to count how many people want the feature behind it.
- [Fake scarcity](https://vocab.design/fake-scarcity.md): Claiming limited supply that is not real, with stock counts or demand messages generated to pressure a decision rather than report a fact.
- [Fake social proof](https://vocab.design/fake-social-proof.md): Manufacturing evidence that other people approve, through invented reviews, testimonials, or live activity messages nobody actually generated.
- [Fake urgency](https://vocab.design/fake-urgency.md): Presenting a deadline that does not exist, usually a timer that resets on reload, so the reader hurries a decision they had time to make.
- [False bottom](https://vocab.design/false-bottom.md): A page that looks finished at a point where content actually continues, so the reader stops scrolling and never sees the rest.
- [Feature gate](https://vocab.design/feature-gate.md): Showing a locked feature in place, with its real position in the interface, so the reader sees what upgrading would unlock rather than a hidden absence.
- [Feature spotlight](https://vocab.design/feature-spotlight.md): A one-time announcement pointing at something newly added, shown in place next to the feature and dismissed for good once acknowledged.
- [First run experience](https://vocab.design/first-run-experience.md): Everything shown only on the very first open, from a welcome sequence to seeded sample content, and never shown to that person again.
- [Forced continuity](https://vocab.design/forced-continuity.md): Turning a free trial into a paid subscription automatically, with the card taken up front and no reminder before the first real charge.
- [Forgiving format](https://vocab.design/forgiving-format.md): Accepting whatever shape the reader types and normalising it afterwards, instead of rejecting input that differs only in spacing or punctuation.
- [Friend spam](https://vocab.design/friend-spam.md): Asking for access to a contact list under one pretext and using it to send invitations that appear to come from the reader.
- [Generative UI](https://vocab.design/generative-ui.md): An interface whose parts are chosen or composed by a model at runtime, so a request is answered with a built form, chart, or panel instead of a paragraph of text.
- [Goal gradient](https://vocab.design/goal-gradient.md): Effort rising as a visible goal gets closer, which is why interfaces show how little is left rather than how much has been done.
- [Gradual engagement](https://vocab.design/gradual-engagement.md): Replacing a sign-up form at the front door with a first useful action, so the reader experiences value before being asked for anything.
- [Guest checkout](https://vocab.design/guest-checkout.md): Letting a buyer complete a purchase without creating an account, with the offer to save details moved to after the order is placed.
- [Help drawer](https://vocab.design/help-drawer.md): Documentation opened beside the task rather than over it, keeping the form usable while the explanation is read and staying open across steps.
- [Honeypot field](https://vocab.design/honeypot-field.md): A form field hidden from people but visible to automated form fillers, used to reject submissions that fill it in without challenging anyone.
- [Hub and spoke](https://vocab.design/hub-and-spoke.md): A navigation shape where every task is reached from one home screen and returns to it, with no way to move sideways between tasks.
- [Hydration](https://vocab.design/hydration.md): The pass where script attaches behaviour to server-rendered HTML, turning a page that is already painted and readable into one that answers input.
- [Infinite scroll](https://vocab.design/infinite-scroll.md): A list that appends the next page of results automatically as the reader approaches the bottom, so the content never ends and no page controls appear.
- [Inline autocomplete](https://vocab.design/inline-autocomplete.md): Completing the reader's text inside the field itself, with the guessed remainder selected so the next keystroke replaces it.
- [Inline validation](https://vocab.design/inline-validation.md): Checking a field as the reader fills or leaves it and showing the verdict beside that field, rather than saving every complaint for the submit button.
- [Interest invoker](https://vocab.design/interest-invoker.md): A link or button that shows more when a reader shows interest in it, by hovering, focusing or long pressing, with no click and no script deciding what interest means.
- [Interface metaphor](https://vocab.design/interface-metaphor.md): Explaining a system by dressing it as something the user already knows: the desktop, the trash can, the folder, the shopping cart.
- [Interstitial](https://vocab.design/interstitial.md): A full screen placed between two steps of a flow, carrying a message, an advert, or a warning that the reader must pass through to continue.
- [Invoker command](https://vocab.design/invoker-command.md): A button that names the element it acts on and what to do to it, in markup, so opening a dialog or toggling a popover needs no script at all.
- [Labor illusion](https://vocab.design/labor-illusion.md): Showing the work a system is doing, or stretching it, so the answer feels earned: the search that lists the sites it is checking instead of answering at once.
- [Lazy loading](https://vocab.design/lazy-loading.md): Deferring the fetch of an image, list section, or module until it is about to be needed, usually when it approaches the viewport.
- [Lazy registration](https://vocab.design/lazy-registration.md): Letting someone use a product and accumulate state anonymously, and asking for an account only when that state needs to survive the session.
- [Leaderboard](https://vocab.design/leaderboard.md): A ranked list of participants by some score, with the reader's own position pinned into view even when it falls outside the visible range.
- [List virtualization](https://vocab.design/list-virtualization.md): Rendering only the rows currently in view and a small buffer around them, while spacers preserve the scrollbar of the full list.
- [Load more](https://vocab.design/load-more.md): A button at the end of a list that fetches and appends the next batch only when pressed, keeping the reader in control of how much arrives.
