- [Magic link](https://vocab.design/magic-link.md): Signing in by clicking a single-use link emailed on request, with no password, and a screen that waits and offers to resend while the mail arrives.
- [Mention autocomplete](https://vocab.design/mention-autocomplete.md): Typing a trigger character inside a text field to open a filtered list of people or objects, inserting the chosen one as a linked token.
- [Metered paywall](https://vocab.design/metered-paywall.md): A paywall that grants a fixed number of free items per period and counts down publicly, so the barrier arrives only after the reader is invested.
- [Microcopy](https://vocab.design/microcopy.md): An interface's smallest strings: the verb on the button, the line under the field, the sentence when it fails. Short enough to be read every time.
- [Microsurvey](https://vocab.design/microsurvey.md): A one or two question survey placed inside the product at the moment being asked about, answered in place rather than on a separate page.
- [Mini cart](https://vocab.design/mini-cart.md): A compact view of the basket opened from the cart icon, confirming what was just added and offering checkout without leaving the current page.
- [Misdirection](https://vocab.design/misdirection.md): Using contrast, size, and position to pull attention to the option the business prefers while the other option is present but visually demoted.
- [Mockup](https://vocab.design/mockup.md): A screen shown as it will look rather than as it will work: colour, type and real copy all settled, and nothing in it clickable.
- [Morphing control](https://vocab.design/morphing-controls.md): One control that changes what it says and does according to state, showing play when paused and pause when playing rather than offering both.
- [Multimodal interface](https://vocab.design/multimodal-interface.md): An interface that accepts and answers in more than one channel at once, letting a person speak, type, touch, or point and pick whichever suits the moment.
- [Nagging](https://vocab.design/nagging.md): Interrupting a task again and again with the same request, so that agreeing becomes the cheapest way to be left alone.
- [Natural language interface](https://vocab.design/natural-language-interface.md): An interface whose input is ordinary language, typed or spoken: the user states an intent in their own words and the system parses it, instead of picking from controls.
- [No results state](https://vocab.design/no-results-state.md): What a search or filtered list shows when nothing matched, naming the query, explaining why, and offering a way to loosen the constraints.
- [Notification digest](https://vocab.design/notification-digest.md): Collecting many similar alerts into one summary rather than delivering each, so the count rises but the number of interruptions does not.
- [Obstruction](https://vocab.design/obstruction.md): Putting deliberate hurdles in front of an action the business does not want taken, so the effort itself does the discouraging.
- [Offline indicator](https://vocab.design/offline-indicator.md): A persistent notice that the product has lost its connection, saying what still works, what is queued, and when the last sync happened.
- [Onboarding checklist](https://vocab.design/onboarding-checklist.md): A persistent list of setup tasks with completion state and a progress meter, kept available so the reader can return to unfinished steps.
- [Onboarding tour](https://vocab.design/onboarding-tour.md): A short sequence of pointers layered over a live interface, each naming one control, advanced by the reader and skippable at any point.
- [One thing per page](https://vocab.design/one-thing-per-page.md): Asking a single question on each screen of a form so the reader never chooses which field to answer first and errors point somewhere unambiguous.
- [One-time code login](https://vocab.design/one-time-code-login.md): Signing in by typing a short code sent to a second channel, keeping the reader inside the app rather than sending them out to a mail client.
- [Operational transparency](https://vocab.design/operational-transparency.md): Showing the work as it happens, the kitchen made visible, so a wait is understood rather than merely endured and the result is trusted more for having been watched.
- [Optimistic UI](https://vocab.design/optimistic-ui.md): Showing the result of an action immediately and reconciling with the server afterward, instead of making the user wait for confirmation.
- [Order summary](https://vocab.design/order-summary.md): The persistent panel beside a checkout listing items, quantities, and every cost line, kept visible so nothing about the total arrives as a surprise.
- [Overloaded command](https://vocab.design/overloaded-command.md): One command word or icon wired to different outcomes depending on where it sits, so having used it once teaches the reader nothing about the next one.
- [Passkey](https://vocab.design/passkey.md): Signing in with a device-held credential unlocked by the reader's own biometric or screen lock, so the interface asks for a face or fingerprint, not a secret.
- [Password strength meter](https://vocab.design/password-strength-meter.md): A gauge that scores a password while it is typed and names what would improve it, replacing a list of rules with continuous feedback.
- [Paywall](https://vocab.design/paywall.md): A barrier that stops access to content or a feature until the reader pays, placed either before anything is shown or partway into the content.
- [Permission priming](https://vocab.design/permission-priming.md): Explaining why access is needed in the product's own dialog first, and only firing the operating system prompt once the reader has said yes to that.
- [Preselected opt-in](https://vocab.design/preselected-opt-in.md): Arriving at a choice with the answer that benefits the business already ticked, so consent is collected from everyone who does not notice.
- [Preview text](https://vocab.design/preview-text.md): The line an inbox prints under a subject, written as hidden text at the top of the mail so the client shows those words instead of scraping whatever body copy comes first.
- [Print stylesheet](https://vocab.design/print-stylesheet.md): The rules that decide what a page becomes on paper: navigation dropped, link targets spelled out, backgrounds abandoned, and the content given page margins.
- [Priority plus navigation](https://vocab.design/priority-plus-navigation.md): A horizontal menu that keeps as many items visible as fit and moves the rest into a More control, recalculating whenever the available width changes.
- [Privacy zuckering](https://vocab.design/privacy-zuckering.md): Steering people into sharing more about themselves than they meant to, by making the permissive choice the easy one and the private choice several clicks deep.
- [Progressive disclosure](https://vocab.design/progressive-disclosure.md): Showing the few options most people need and keeping the rest one deliberate step away, so complexity arrives only when it is asked for.
- [Progressive image loading](https://vocab.design/progressive-image-loading.md): Showing a cheap stand-in for an image, a blur, a dominant colour, or a low resolution copy, and swapping in the full file once it arrives.
- [Progressive profiling](https://vocab.design/progressive-profiling.md): Collecting profile details a few at a time across separate visits, instead of demanding the whole record in one long form at registration.
- [Progressive reduction](https://vocab.design/progressive-reduction.md): Simplifying a control as the same person uses it more, dropping the label once the icon has been learned and restoring it after a long absence.
- [Prototype](https://vocab.design/prototype.md): A design wired up just enough to be tried: screens linked so that a tap goes somewhere, with nothing real behind the links.
- [Pull to refresh](https://vocab.design/pull-to-refresh.md): Dragging a list downward past its top edge to trigger a reload, with an indicator that appears in the space the drag opens up.
- [Quick return header](https://vocab.design/quick-return-header.md): A header that slides out of the way while the reader scrolls down and returns immediately on the first upward scroll, without waiting for the top of the page.
- [Quick view](https://vocab.design/quick-view.md): Opening a summary of an item over the list it came from, so the reader can inspect it and return without losing scroll position or filters.
- [Rage click](https://vocab.design/rage-click.md): A burst of repeated clicks on one spot, the shape frustration takes when a control answers nothing, and the analytics signal that goes looking for it.
- [Rating prompt](https://vocab.design/rating-prompt.md): An in-product request to rate or review, usually timed to a moment of success and often filtered so only positive responses reach the public store.
- [Read receipt](https://vocab.design/read-receipt.md): A per-message marker reporting how far a message got, sent, delivered, or read, drawn as ticks, labels, or the recipient's avatar.
- [Reading progress](https://vocab.design/reading-progress.md): A bar tied to scroll position that shows how much of an article remains, usually pinned to the top edge and filling as the reader descends.
- [Recurring event](https://vocab.design/recurring-event.md): An event stored once as a rule instead of as copies, so every second Tuesday can be edited, skipped for one week, or ended, without touching the rest.
- [Roach motel](https://vocab.design/roach-motel.md): Making entry into a commitment take one click and exit take a phone call, a chat queue, or a buried page, so the asymmetry keeps people subscribed.
- [Rule builder](https://vocab.design/rule-builder.md): Assembling a condition from dropdowns and values, joined by and or or, so a non-programmer can express a query without writing one.
- [Save for later](https://vocab.design/save-for-later.md): Moving an item out of the active list into a parked list that stays associated with the reader, without deleting it or committing to it.
- [Scarcity indicator](https://vocab.design/scarcity-indicator.md): A label reporting how little of something is left, in stock, in seats, or in time, placed beside the action it is meant to accelerate.
- [Scroll edge fade](https://vocab.design/scroll-edge-fade.md): A gradient mask at the edge of a scroll container that fades clipped content out, hinting that more lies past the edge without drawing a control.
- [Scroll hijacking](https://vocab.design/scroll-hijacking.md): Overriding the browser's scrolling so a wheel turn advances a scripted sequence instead of moving the page by the distance the reader asked for.
- [Scroll spy](https://vocab.design/scroll-spy.md): Navigation that watches the scroll position and highlights the entry for the section currently in view.
- [Scrollytelling](https://vocab.design/scrollytelling.md): A narrative layout where a pinned graphic stays fixed while text scrolls past it, each step changing what the graphic shows.
- [Select all across pages](https://vocab.design/select-all-across-pages.md): Offering to extend a selection from the visible page to every matching row, after a header checkbox has selected only what is on screen.
- [Sender name](https://vocab.design/sender-name.md): The name a mail appears to come from, chosen rather than inherited, because a reader scanning an inbox decides on it before reading a word of the subject.
- [Skeleton screen](https://vocab.design/skeleton-screen.md): A loading state made of grey shapes standing where the content will be, showing the layout before the data arrives.
- [Slash command](https://vocab.design/slash-command.md): Typing a forward slash in a composer to open a menu of actions, where choosing one runs it rather than inserting the words into the message.
- [Smart app banner](https://vocab.design/smart-app-banner.md): A strip pinned to the top of a mobile web page urging the reader to open or install the native app instead, with an install or open action.
- [Smart defaults](https://vocab.design/smart-defaults.md): Prefilling a choice with the answer most people in this situation want, so the common case needs no work and every other case is still reachable.
- [Sneak into basket](https://vocab.design/sneak-into-basket.md): Adding an item the buyer never chose, an insurance, a donation, a warranty, into the cart through a preselected control found earlier in the flow.
- [Social login](https://vocab.design/social-login.md): Signing in by delegating identity to an existing account elsewhere, presented as a row of provider buttons above or instead of a password form.
- [Social proof](https://vocab.design/social-proof.md): Showing what other people did or said next to a decision, as counts, reviews, logos, or live activity, so the reader can borrow their judgement.
- [Soft delete](https://vocab.design/soft-delete.md): Removing an item from view but keeping it recoverable in a trash or archive for a period, so deletion is reversible without a confirmation step.
- [Speculative loading](https://vocab.design/speculative-loading.md): Fetching, or fully rendering, a page before the reader asks for it, on a guess about where they go next, so the navigation is already done when the click lands.
- [Steps left](https://vocab.design/steps-left.md): Telling the reader where they are in a multi step task and how many steps are still to come, so the end of the task is visible from the start.
- [Sticky add to cart](https://vocab.design/sticky-add-to-cart.md): A condensed product bar that pins itself to an edge once the real buy button has scrolled away, keeping price and purchase always reachable.
- [Stories](https://vocab.design/stories.md): A sequence of full-screen cards that advance on a timer, paused by holding, skipped by tapping the edges, and gone after a fixed lifetime.
- [Streak](https://vocab.design/streak.md): A count of consecutive periods in which the reader did the thing, displayed prominently and lost if a period is missed.
- [Structured format](https://vocab.design/structured-format.md): Splitting one value across several small fields with fixed shapes, which teaches the expected format but costs the reader extra focus moves.
- [Styled alt text](https://vocab.design/styled-alt-text.md): Alt text given size, colour and weight so a mail whose images are blocked still reads as something designed instead of as a column of grey stubs.
- [Subject line](https://vocab.design/subject-line.md): The one line a mail is opened or ignored on, written to survive a list that truncates it and shows it wedged between the sender and the preview text.
- [Swipe deck](https://vocab.design/swipe-deck.md): A stack of cards judged one at a time, each thrown left or right to record a binary decision and reveal the next card underneath.
- [Swipe to dismiss](https://vocab.design/swipe-to-dismiss.md): Flinging an item off the edge of the screen to remove it, with the item tracking the finger and snapping back if the throw is too short.
- [Table of contents](https://vocab.design/table-of-contents.md): A list of a document's sections, linked in reading order, shown beside or above the text.
- [Time zone display](https://vocab.design/time-zone-display.md): Whose clock a time is shown on, the reader's or the event's, and saying which, because a time with no zone beside it is a meeting somebody is going to miss.
- [Transactional email](https://vocab.design/transactional-email.md): Mail sent because one person did one thing, a receipt or a reset, which is why it may carry no marketing and why its design is a record rather than a pitch.
- [Trick wording](https://vocab.design/trick-wording.md): Phrasing a choice so its plain reading is the opposite of its effect, typically through double negatives or a label that describes the wrong outcome.
- [Truncated axis](https://vocab.design/truncated-axis.md): Starting a value axis above zero so differences look bigger than they are; honest for lines and dots, a lie for bars.
- [Type to confirm](https://vocab.design/type-to-confirm.md): Guarding a destructive action by making the reader type the name of the thing being destroyed before the confirm button becomes usable.
- [Typeahead](https://vocab.design/typeahead.md): Offering suggestions that update on every keystroke, drawn from a live query, so the reader picks a result rather than finishing the phrase.
- [Undo](https://vocab.design/undo.md): Letting an action run immediately and offering to reverse it afterwards, instead of stopping to ask whether the reader really meant it.
- [Unsaved changes guard](https://vocab.design/unsaved-changes-guard.md): Warning the reader that edits will be lost before a navigation or close is allowed to proceed, and offering to save or discard first.
- [Unsubscribe link](https://vocab.design/unsubscribe-link.md): The way out of a mailing list, which the law and the mail clients now both insist is one click, and whose difficulty is the honest measure of a sender.
- [Wireframe](https://vocab.design/wireframe.md): A screen drawn as structure only: blocks where the content goes, a crossed box for an image, ruled lines for text, with no colour or type decided yet.
- [Zero state](https://vocab.design/zero-state.md): The first-run screen a feature shows before any data exists, written to teach the feature rather than to report emptiness.
- [Zero UI](https://vocab.design/zero-ui.md): A paradigm where the screen stops being the interface and the interaction happens through voice, gesture, presence, or sensors, so the system responds without anything to look at.

## aesthetic

- [Acid graphics](https://vocab.design/acid-graphics.md): A 2020s rave revival style of chrome and liquid 3D objects, warped and stretched lettering, clashing saturated colour on near black, smileys, globes, and wireframe motifs.
- [Afrofuturism](https://vocab.design/afrofuturism.md): A style that pictures technology through the African diaspora, combining cosmic imagery, textile and mask pattern, gold and indigo, and geometric ornament used structurally.
- [Anti-design](https://vocab.design/anti-design.md): A deliberately awkward style that breaks layout, type, and color conventions so the interface reads as a statement rather than as a polished product.
- [Aqua](https://vocab.design/aqua.md): Apple's early Mac OS X look of glossy blue gel buttons, pinstripes, gumdrop window controls, and a pulsing default button.
- [Art Deco](https://vocab.design/art-deco.md): A 1920s luxury style of strict symmetry, stepped and fanned geometry, strong vertical emphasis, metallic gold on deep colour, and high contrast display capitals.
- [Art Nouveau](https://vocab.design/art-nouveau.md): A turn of the century style of whiplash curves, botanical line ornament, muted jewel tones, and lettering drawn to fit the frame rather than set on a grid.
- [Aurora UI](https://vocab.design/aurora-ui.md): A style whose background is built from heavily blurred color blobs that glow and drift like the northern lights behind the content.
- [Bauhaus style](https://vocab.design/bauhaus-style.md): A style reduced to primary red, yellow, and blue on off-white, elementary circles, triangles, and squares, and undecorated sans serif type.
- [Biophilic design](https://vocab.design/biophilic-design.md): A style that borrows from the natural world on purpose, using earthy greens and clays, organic silhouettes, botanical imagery, and slow ambient motion to make a screen feel less mechanical.
- [Brutalist web design](https://vocab.design/brutalist-web-design.md): A raw style that leaves the document showing: system or monospace type, default link blue, hard borders, and no decoration beyond structure.
- [Cassette futurism](https://vocab.design/cassette-futurism.md): The analog future of late 1970s science fiction: beige and putty plastic, chunky toggles and rocker switches, amber or green CRT readouts, and monochrome bitmap type.
- [Claymorphism](https://vocab.design/claymorphism.md): A soft style where controls look inflated from clay: pastel fills, very large corner radii, an inner highlight, and a tinted drop shadow.
- [Constructivism](https://vocab.design/constructivism.md): A 1920s poster language of diagonal bars and blocks, red and black on off-white, photomontage, and heavy sans capitals set on a strong angle.
- [Corporate Memphis](https://vocab.design/corporate-memphis.md): The flat vector illustration style of bright, faceless people with long bendy limbs and small torsos that spread across tech marketing from 2017.
- [Cyberpunk UI](https://vocab.design/cyberpunk-ui.md): A dystopian sci-fi interface style: near-black surfaces, one or two toxic neon accents, monospace all-caps labels, clipped corners, and scanline or glitch noise laid over the top.
- [De Stijl](https://vocab.design/de-stijl.md): A style built only from black rules, rectangular fields, and the three primaries on white, arranged asymmetrically with no curves and no diagonals.
- [Digital collage](https://vocab.design/digital-collage.md): A composition assembled from cut-out photography, torn paper edges, scanned texture, and type set at odd angles, so the page reads as pasted up rather than laid out.
- [Digital rain](https://vocab.design/digital-rain.md): Columns of glyphs falling and trailing away, green on black, the Matrix screen quoted so often that it now reads as shorthand for a computer thinking.
- [E-ink aesthetic](https://vocab.design/e-ink-aesthetic.md): A paper-like style built for or borrowed from electronic ink: near-white ground, pure black text, hairline rules, no shadows or gradients, and paged navigation.
- [Editorial web design](https://vocab.design/editorial-web-design.md): A style that borrows print magazine craft for the screen: a visible column grid, display type at poster scale, pull quotes, rules, and captioned images set into the text.
- [Fictional user interface](https://vocab.design/fictional-user-interface.md): The screen graphics style invented for film, television, and games: dense readouts, targeting reticles, and animated telemetry that look computational without computing anything.
- [Flat 2.0](https://vocab.design/flat-design-2.md): Flat design with the depth cues put back in small doses: soft shadow, subtle gradient, and hover feedback that show what can actually be clicked.
- [Flat design](https://vocab.design/flat-design.md): A style that strips away depth cues, using solid fills, sharp edges, and bold color instead of shadow, gradient, bevel, or texture.
- [Frutiger Aero](https://vocab.design/frutiger-aero.md): The mid 2000s look of glossy gradients, bubbles, water, bright skies, and clean humanist type, named after the typeface and Windows Aero.
- [Frutiger Metro](https://vocab.design/frutiger-metro.md): The flat vector cousin of Frutiger Aero: gradient color blocks, bloom and glow, silhouetted figures, swooshes and abstract flourishes, without the glossy water and grass.
- [Glassmorphism](https://vocab.design/glassmorphism.md): A style where surfaces are translucent and blur what is behind them, separated from the backdrop by a hairline edge and a soft shadow.
- [Glitch aesthetic](https://vocab.design/glitch-aesthetic.md): A look that fakes signal failure with colour channel offset, torn scan bands, and jitter, used for emphasis or as a whole visual identity.
- [Grunge design](https://vocab.design/grunge-design.md): A 1990s style of torn and photocopied texture, overlapped and cut type, off-grid layout, and dirty muted colour, where legibility is traded for emotional pitch.
- [Hand-drawn UI](https://vocab.design/hand-drawn-ui.md): A style whose lines wobble as if sketched by hand, used to signal that a diagram or wireframe is provisional rather than finished.
- [Hyperreal 3D](https://vocab.design/hyperreal-3d.md): Rendered objects pushed past photographic realism, with physically based materials, sharp specular detail, and studio lighting, floated over an otherwise plain interface.
- [Isometric illustration](https://vocab.design/isometric-illustration.md): Art drawn on a fixed axonometric grid so depth reads without perspective, with parallel edges and no vanishing point.
- [Kawaii UI](https://vocab.design/kawaii-ui.md): A cute style of pastel fills, rounded everything, oversized eyes and blush marks, sticker and mascot characters, and hand-lettered or bubbly rounded type.
- [Liquid Glass](https://vocab.design/liquid-glass.md): Apple's 2025 material where controls float as a translucent layer that refracts what is behind them and reshapes fluidly as content moves underneath.
- [Low poly](https://vocab.design/low-poly.md): A 3D style that keeps the polygon count low enough to see, so surfaces read as faceted triangles under flat shading instead of smooth curves.
- [Material 3 Expressive](https://vocab.design/material-3-expressive.md): Google's 2025 update to Material 3: springier motion, emphasized typography, updated dynamic colour themes, and responsive components that stretch to hug the display.
- [Material You](https://vocab.design/material-you.md): Google's personalization layer where the system derives an app's entire color scheme from the user's wallpaper, so every app shifts together.
- [Maximalism](https://vocab.design/maximalism.md): A style that fills the screen on purpose with layered color, pattern, and type, treating abundance rather than restraint as the message.
- [Memphis design](https://vocab.design/memphis-design.md): The 1980s Memphis Group look of clashing pastels, squiggles, confetti dots, and terrazzo shapes scattered across a layout.
- [Metro](https://vocab.design/metro-design.md): Microsoft's typography led design language of flat coloured tiles, large light headings, and motion used in place of chrome, shadow, and texture.
- [Mica](https://vocab.design/mica.md): Fluent's opaque app background material, subtly tinted with the user's desktop wallpaper colour and going neutral when the window loses focus.
- [Mid-century modern](https://vocab.design/mid-century-modern.md): A 1950s and 60s style of muted mustard, teal, and burnt orange, tapered organic shapes, textured paper grounds, and friendly geometric sans type.
- [Minimalism](https://vocab.design/minimalism.md): A style that reduces an interface to one typeface, one accent color, and generous empty space, letting whitespace rather than ornament carry hierarchy.
- [Neo-skeuomorphism](https://vocab.design/neo-skeuomorphism.md): The current return of depth and material to interfaces, using restrained texture, shadow, and highlight instead of literal leather, metal, and felt.
- [Neubrutalism](https://vocab.design/neubrutalism.md): A loud style built from thick black outlines, saturated flat color, square corners, and hard offset shadows with zero blur.
- [Neumorphism](https://vocab.design/neumorphism.md): A style where controls look extruded from or pressed into one background colour, shaped only by soft light and shadow.
- [New Wave design](https://vocab.design/new-wave-design.md): The postmodern break from Swiss order: stair-stepped rules, diagonal and letter-spaced type, weights mixed inside a word, and text reversed out of bars.
- [Pixel art UI](https://vocab.design/pixel-art-ui.md): An interface drawn on a visible pixel grid, with bitmap type, hard aliased edges, and icons kept at their original low resolution.
- [Pop art style](https://vocab.design/pop-art-style.md): A comic and advertising style of flat primary color, heavy black outlines, printed dot shading, speech balloons, and bold condensed capitals.
- [Psychedelic style](https://vocab.design/psychedelic-style.md): A 1960s poster style of vibrating complementary color, warped and interlocking lettering that fills its own shape, kaleidoscopic symmetry, and liquid distortion.
- [Retro film aesthetic](https://vocab.design/retro-film-aesthetic.md): A treatment that makes digital imagery look shot on film, adding grain, halation, light leaks, faded contrast, dust, and sometimes a corner date stamp.
- [Retro web design](https://vocab.design/retro-web-design.md): A style that rebuilds the early desktop web on purpose: beveled window chrome, pixel and system type, garish color, and animated banners.
- [Retro-futurism](https://vocab.design/retro-futurism.md): A style that pictures the future the way an earlier decade pictured it, so the technology shown is advanced but the type, color, and hardware belong to the past.
- [Risograph style](https://vocab.design/risograph.md): A print-inspired look of two or three flat spot colors that misregister slightly and show grain, imitating a riso duplicator.
- [Skeuomorphism](https://vocab.design/skeuomorphism.md): A style that makes interface elements imitate real objects and materials, using leather, metal, paper, and glossy highlights so their purpose reads as familiar.
- [Solarpunk](https://vocab.design/solarpunk.md): An optimistic ecological future style of daylight palettes, plant growth over structure, stained glass colour, art nouveau curves, and visible solar and wind technology.
- [Spatial UI](https://vocab.design/spatial-ui.md): Interface designed to sit in three dimensional space, where panels are made of a system glass material and hierarchy is carried by depth rather than by colour.
- [Steampunk](https://vocab.design/steampunk.md): A Victorian industrial style of brass, riveted plate, wood, and leather, with gauges, cogs, and valve controls standing in for ordinary interface widgets.
- [Swiss style](https://vocab.design/swiss-style.md): The Swiss modernist system of a strict grid, flush left sans serif type, asymmetric layout, and objective photography, still the base of clean UI layout.
- [Synthwave](https://vocab.design/synthwave.md): A neon 1980s look built on sunset gradients, glowing perspective grids, and chrome type, close to vaporwave but sincere rather than ironic.
- [Terminal aesthetic](https://vocab.design/terminal-aesthetic.md): A look borrowed from the command line: monospace type on a fixed character grid, a block cursor, and green or amber text on black.
- [Vaporwave](https://vocab.design/vaporwave.md): A retro internet look of magenta and cyan gradients, grid horizons, Japanese type, statuary, and 90s desktop chrome used ironically.
- [Vernacular web](https://vocab.design/vernacular-web.md): The amateur homepage look of the GeoCities era: tiled backgrounds, sparkle GIFs, under construction signs, midi music, and hit counters.
- [VHS aesthetic](https://vocab.design/vhs-aesthetic.md): A look that imitates a worn videotape: tracking bands, smeared color bleeding past edges, interlace comb artifacts, and burned-in timecode or REC overlays.
- [Windows Aero](https://vocab.design/windows-aero.md): The Windows Vista and 7 look built on translucent glass window frames, soft outer glows, reflections, and animated window transitions.
- [Y2K aesthetic](https://vocab.design/y2k-aesthetic.md): The turn of the millennium look of chrome type, bubble shapes, translucent plastic, and lens flares, revived as a web and app style.

## interaction

- [Access key](https://vocab.design/access-key.md): A single letter, usually shown underlined, that jumps straight to a menu or control once the access modifier is held.
- [Affordance](https://vocab.design/affordance.md): What an element makes possible for the person using it, such as a surface that can be pushed, dragged, or scrolled.
- [Auditory icon](https://vocab.design/auditory-icon.md): A recorded everyday sound standing for an event, so a crumple means delete by resembling the act rather than by convention learned in the interface.
- [Brushing](https://vocab.design/brushing.md): Dragging a selection across one chart to highlight the same records in every linked view.
- [Caret](https://vocab.design/caret.md): The blinking marker showing where typed text will be inserted, moved by clicking, by arrow keys, or by dragging on touch.
- [Chorded shortcut](https://vocab.design/chorded-shortcut.md): A shortcut whose keys are held down together like a chord, in contrast to one typed as a sequence of separate presses.
- [Click-through](https://vocab.design/click-through.md): A click that both focuses an inactive surface and reaches the control underneath, instead of being spent activating the window first.
- [Context menu](https://vocab.design/context-menu.md): A menu of actions for one specific object, opened on that object by right click, long press, or the context menu key.
- [Dead zone](https://vocab.design/dead-zone.md): A range of input near the resting position that is deliberately ignored, so tiny unintended movement produces no response at all.
- [Debounce](https://vocab.design/debounce.md): Waiting until input has stopped for a set moment before reacting, so a burst of keystrokes or clicks produces one response instead of many.
- [Detent](https://vocab.design/detent.md): A position a control settles into and resists leaving, so a continuous drag or turn lands on discrete values that can be felt rather than read.
- [Double click](https://vocab.design/double-click.md): Two clicks inside a short interval on the same spot, treated as one gesture that opens, edits, or selects a word rather than activating twice.
- [Double tap](https://vocab.design/double-tap.md): Two taps in quick succession on the same spot, conventionally used to zoom in on content or to zoom back out when already zoomed.
- [Drag and drop](https://vocab.design/drag-and-drop.md): Picking up an object, moving it under continuous pointer or finger contact, and releasing it over a target that accepts it.
- [Drag autoscroll](https://vocab.design/drag-autoscroll.md): Scrolling a container automatically when a drag is held near its edge, so an item can be moved somewhere currently off screen.
- [Drag threshold](https://vocab.design/drag-threshold.md): The small distance a pointer must travel while pressed before the gesture counts as a drag, so a shaky click is not mistaken for one.
- [Drag to create](https://vocab.design/drag-to-create.md): Making a new object by dragging out its extent rather than pressing Add: an event drawn across two hours, a frame drawn on a canvas, a range drawn on a chart.
- [Drop zone](https://vocab.design/drop-zone.md): The region that will accept a dragged item, usually highlighted while a compatible drag is in flight so the destination is unmistakable.
- [Dwell activation](https://vocab.design/dwell-activation.md): Committing an action by keeping a pointer or gaze still on a target for a set time, for input methods that have no click of their own.
- [Earcon](https://vocab.design/earcon.md): A brief synthesized sound standing for an event, abstract by design, so a rising figure means success only because the interface taught you it does.
- [Easter egg](https://vocab.design/easter-egg.md): A reward hidden behind an action nobody was told about, put there to be found rather than to be used.
- [Edge swipe](https://vocab.design/edge-swipe.md): A swipe that begins off the screen edge and travels inward, reserved by the system for navigation such as going back or revealing a drawer.
- [Feedforward](https://vocab.design/feedforward.md): What an interface says about the result of an act before it is taken, the half of the loop that sits ahead of the action rather than after it.
- [Fitts's law](https://vocab.design/fitts-law.md): The rule that the time to hit a target grows with its distance and shrinks with its size, which is why screen edges and corners are so easy to reach.
- [Fling](https://vocab.design/fling.md): The fastest of the drag family: contact is released while it is still moving, so the content keeps travelling and the gesture cannot be dragged back.
- [Focus follows mouse](https://vocab.design/focus-follows-mouse.md): A focus model in which whatever the pointer is over receives keyboard input, without any click to claim it first.
- [Force touch](https://vocab.design/force-touch.md): A press whose depth is part of the input, letting a harder press mean something different from a light one on a pressure sensing surface.
- [Ghost click](https://vocab.design/ghost-click.md): A stray click the browser emits after a touch has already been handled, landing on whatever moved under the finger in the meantime.
- [Haptic feedback](https://vocab.design/haptic-feedback.md): A brief physical vibration or tap produced by the device to confirm an interaction, mark a boundary, or signal success and failure.
- [Hidden gesture](https://vocab.design/hidden-gesture.md): An action reachable only by an input the reader has to guess: a swipe, a long press, a two-finger tap, with nothing on screen saying it is there.
- [Hit slop](https://vocab.design/hit-slop.md): Invisible padding that extends a control's activatable area beyond its drawn bounds, so a small icon can stay small and still be easy to hit.
- [Hit testing](https://vocab.design/hit-testing.md): Working out which element sits under a pointer, which decides who receives the event when shapes overlap or transparent areas are in the way.
- [Hold to confirm](https://vocab.design/hold-to-confirm.md): Requiring a press to be held for a moment before a destructive action commits, with progress shown so the wait is understood as deliberate.
- [Hover](https://vocab.design/hover.md): A pointer resting over an element without pressing, a state that exists for mice and pens but has no true equivalent on touch.
- [Hover intent](https://vocab.design/hover-intent.md): Waiting out a short delay or watching cursor direction before acting on a hover, so a pointer merely passing through does not open anything.
- [Juiciness](https://vocab.design/juiciness.md): Stacking far more feedback on an act than it needs, so one small input wobbles, pops and sings, and the interface feels alive under the hand.
- [Key repeat](https://vocab.design/key-repeat.md): A held key firing repeatedly after an initial delay, which is how arrow keys scroll and backspace deletes more than one character.
- [Key sequence](https://vocab.design/key-sequence.md): A shortcut typed as an ordered run of presses, where the first key opens a mode and the next chooses within it.
- [Keyboard shortcut](https://vocab.design/keyboard-shortcut.md): A key or key combination that runs a command directly, giving practised users a path that skips the menus and the pointer entirely.
- [Lasso selection](https://vocab.design/lasso-selection.md): Selecting by dragging a boundary around items on a canvas, freehand or as a rectangle, so whatever the outline encloses becomes the selection when the drag ends.
- [Light dismiss](https://vocab.design/light-dismiss.md): Closing a transient surface by clicking outside it or pressing Escape, without a dedicated close control being used.
- [Long press](https://vocab.design/long-press.md): A press held in place for a moment before release, used to reveal secondary actions, enter a rearrange mode, or open a contextual menu.
- [Look and pinch](https://vocab.design/look-and-pinch.md): Spatial input where the eyes choose the target and a finger pinch commits the action, so selection and activation come from different body parts.
- [Marking menu](https://vocab.design/marking-menu.md): A radial menu that can be answered before it appears: waiting shows the menu, while a confident stroke in the item's direction selects it outright.
- [Microinteraction](https://vocab.design/microinteraction.md): A small self-contained loop of trigger, rule, feedback, and result, such as a toggle that flips, buzzes, and settles into its new state.
- [Middle click](https://vocab.design/middle-click.md): A press of the scroll wheel button, conventionally used to open a link in a new tab, close a tab, or start autoscrolling.
- [Modifier key](https://vocab.design/modifier-key.md): A key held to change what another input means, so the same click or keystroke can copy instead of move, or add instead of replace.
- [Momentum scrolling](https://vocab.design/momentum-scrolling.md): Content that keeps moving after the finger lifts, decelerating as though it had mass, so one flick can travel a long way.
- [Mouse gesture](https://vocab.design/mouse-gesture.md): A command issued by the shape of a pointer stroke, usually with a button held, so a movement stands in for a menu choice.
- [Multi-touch](https://vocab.design/multi-touch.md): Input from more than one simultaneous contact point, letting a surface distinguish two-finger scrolling, pinching, rotating and larger finger counts.
- [Nudge](https://vocab.design/nudge.md): Moving or changing a value by one small fixed step with an arrow key, with a modifier switching to a larger step.
- [Orbit](https://vocab.design/orbit.md): Rotating a camera around a fixed point by dragging, so the scene appears to turn while the subject stays centred.
- [Overscroll](https://vocab.design/overscroll.md): Scrolling input that continues after a scroller has reached its limit, which platforms answer with a bounce, a glow, or a handoff to the parent.
- [Pan](https://vocab.design/pan.md): Moving the viewport across content in any direction while keeping contact, so the content feels anchored to the finger or cursor.
- [Pinch to zoom](https://vocab.design/pinch-to-zoom.md): Two fingers moving apart or together on a surface to scale content up or down, with the scale tracking the distance between them.
- [Pointer capture](https://vocab.design/pointer-capture.md): Redirecting all events for one pointer to a chosen element, so a drag keeps reaching the control it started on even when it wanders off.
- [Pointer lock](https://vocab.design/pointer-lock.md): Hiding the cursor and reading only its movement deltas, so input keeps flowing past the edges of the screen instead of stopping at them.
- [Press-drag-release](https://vocab.design/press-drag-release.md): Operating a menu in one gesture: pressing the trigger opens it, dragging moves through the items while the button stays down, and releasing over an item commits it.
- [Pressed state](https://vocab.design/pressed-state.md): The look a control takes while it is actually being held down, confirming that the press was received before the action runs.
- [Pressure sensitivity](https://vocab.design/pressure-sensitivity.md): Reading how hard a pen or finger presses, plus tilt and twist, so stroke weight and behaviour vary with the shape of the contact.
- [Quasimode](https://vocab.design/quasimode.md): A temporary mode held open by the user, such as a key kept down, so it cannot be forgotten and ends the moment the hold ends.
- [Range select](https://vocab.design/range-select.md): Choosing a contiguous run of items by marking one end and holding Shift while marking the other, selecting everything between them.
- [Rotate gesture](https://vocab.design/rotate-gesture.md): Two fingers turning around a common center to rotate the object or view beneath them, the angle tracking the fingers as they orbit.
- [Roving tabindex](https://vocab.design/roving-tabindex.md): A focus technique where only one item in a group is in the tab order and arrow keys move that position, so Tab enters and leaves the whole group once.
- [Scroll anchoring](https://vocab.design/scroll-anchoring.md): Keeping the reader's position fixed when content loads or resizes above it, by adjusting scroll offset so the visible text does not jump.
- [Scroll chaining](https://vocab.design/scroll-chaining.md): When an inner scroller reaches its end and the gesture continues, the scroll passes to the page behind it unless that handoff is blocked.
- [Scroll lock](https://vocab.design/scroll-lock.md): Freezing the page behind an open overlay so a wheel or swipe moves the overlay's own content and never the document underneath.
- [Scrubbing](https://vocab.design/scrubbing.md): Dragging a playhead along a timeline to move through media by hand, previewing frames as the position changes rather than waiting for playback.
- [Scrubby slider](https://vocab.design/scrubby-slider.md): A numeric field whose label can be dragged sideways to change the value, giving a slider's feel without a slider taking up room.
- [Secondary click](https://vocab.design/secondary-click.md): The alternate pointer press, usually the right button or a two-finger tap, reserved for opening contextual actions rather than activating.
- [Selection follows focus](https://vocab.design/selection-follows-focus.md): A widget where moving focus also selects, so arrowing through tabs or a listbox changes the selection immediately rather than on a second press.
- [Selection handle](https://vocab.design/selection-handle.md): The draggable grip at each end of a touch text selection, used to widen or narrow the range a finger cannot adjust precisely.
- [Shake to undo](https://vocab.design/shake-to-undo.md): Physically shaking a device to trigger undo or redo, an accelerometer gesture Apple defines system wide for reversing a recent edit.
- [Signifier](https://vocab.design/signifier.md): The visible cue that advertises an affordance, such as a grip texture, an underline, or a shadow that says this can be pressed.
- [Slide to confirm](https://vocab.design/slide-to-confirm.md): A control that commits only once its thumb is dragged the length of its track, so the effort of the gesture is the guard against doing it by accident.
- [Smart guides](https://vocab.design/smart-guides.md): Alignment lines that appear only while dragging, showing which edges or centers the moving object currently lines up with.
- [Snapping](https://vocab.design/snapping.md): Pulling a dragged object into exact alignment once it comes within a small distance of a grid, guide, or another object's edge.
- [Spring loading](https://vocab.design/spring-loading.md): Hovering a dragged item over a container until it opens, so a drag can travel through nested destinations without being dropped and restarted.
- [Sticky hover](https://vocab.design/sticky-hover.md): A hover style that stays applied on a touch device after a tap, because there is no pointer to leave and clear the state.
- [Swipe](https://vocab.design/swipe.md): A quick directional drag of a finger across the screen, faster and coarser than a drag, usually without a specific on-screen target.
- [Swipe actions](https://vocab.design/swipe-actions.md): Buttons hidden behind a list row that a partial sideways swipe reveals, so destructive or common actions live under the item itself.
- [Tap](https://vocab.design/tap.md): A single press and lift of one finger on a touch surface, the touch equivalent of a click, used to activate a control or select an item.
- [Tap delay](https://vocab.design/tap-delay.md): The pause a touch browser once held before dispatching a click, kept open in case a second tap arrived and turned the gesture into a zoom.
- [Throttle](https://vocab.design/throttle.md): Capping how often a continuous stream of input is acted on, so a response fires at a steady rate instead of on every event.
- [Touch target](https://vocab.design/touch-target.md): The area of a control that answers a press, padded out around whatever is drawn so a fingertip can hit it without catching its neighbours.

## motion

- [3D tilt](https://vocab.design/tilt-effect.md): Rotating a card in perspective toward the pointer so it appears to tip in three dimensions, often with a moving highlight to sell the depth.
- [Additive animation](https://vocab.design/additive-animation.md): Composing an animation on top of whatever is already animating the same property instead of replacing it, so a second nudge adds to the first rather than restarting it.
- [Anticipation](https://vocab.design/anticipation.md): A small move in the opposite direction just before the main one, borrowed from character animation to telegraph what is about to happen.
- [Arc motion](https://vocab.design/arc-motion.md): Moving an element along a curved path rather than a straight line, so a change of position reads as natural rather than mechanical.
- [Asymmetric easing](https://vocab.design/asymmetric-easing.md): Giving a state change and its reverse different curves or durations, usually a quick confident exit and a slower entrance, so the two directions do not feel identical.
- [Attract mode](https://vocab.design/attract-mode.md): A self-playing loop an idle screen falls into to demonstrate itself, inherited from arcade cabinets and reused by kiosks and product demos.
- [Bounce](https://vocab.design/bounce-animation.md): Motion that arrives, rebounds, and arrives again in decreasing amounts, reading as an object landing on a surface.
- [Card flip](https://vocab.design/card-flip.md): Rotating a card about its own axis to show a second face on the back, with the hidden face pre-rotated and its backface hidden so only one side is ever visible.
- [Cloning](https://vocab.design/cloning.md): Spawning a new element visibly out of an existing one so the reader can see where it came from, rather than having it arrive from nowhere.
- [Collapsing toolbar](https://vocab.design/collapsing-toolbar.md): A header that shrinks as the page scrolls, trading its large title and image for a compact bar that stays available.
- [Compositor-only animation](https://vocab.design/compositor-animation.md): An animation limited to properties the compositor can handle alone, usually transform and opacity, so it keeps running even when the main thread is busy.
- [Confetti burst](https://vocab.design/confetti-burst.md): A short particle celebration thrown across the screen to mark a completion, decorative by design and the first thing reduced motion should drop.
- [Container transform](https://vocab.design/container-transform.md): Material's transition in which a container grows or shrinks into another one, its contents crossfading inside, so a card visibly becomes the screen it opened.
- [Count-up animation](https://vocab.design/count-up-animation.md): Animating a number toward its value instead of setting it, often with digits rolling like an odometer so the change is legible.
- [Crossfade](https://vocab.design/crossfade.md): A transition in which one element fades out while the other fades in over the same span, so both are partly visible at the midpoint.
- [Cubic bezier](https://vocab.design/cubic-bezier.md): The four-control-point curve that describes how a value moves between its start and end, the default way CSS spells an easing.
- [Cursor follower](https://vocab.design/cursor-follower.md): A dot or ring that trails the pointer with a lag and often swells over links, replacing or augmenting the native cursor as a piece of brand motion.
- [Damping](https://vocab.design/damping.md): The friction term in a spring that decides how quickly oscillation dies out, from a loose wobble to a critically damped move with no bounce at all.
- [Deformable UI](https://vocab.design/deformable-ui.md): A style where controls behave like soft matter, squashing under a press and springing back past rest, so the surface reads as jelly, clay, or inflated plastic rather than paint.
- [Delay](https://vocab.design/delay.md): The wait between an animation being triggered and starting to move, the unit a stagger is built from and the difference between twitchy and considered.
- [Dimensionality](https://vocab.design/dimensionality.md): Giving interface objects a believable place in depth by folding, layering or flipping them, so a reader can tell where something went and where it will come back from.
- [Directionality](https://vocab.design/directionality.md): The rule that every movement carries a direction, and that using it consistently tells the reader how the parts of an interface relate.
- [Dissolve](https://vocab.design/dissolve.md): A fade that carries the eye from one image or state to another without any movement, inherited from film editing vocabulary.
- [Dock magnification](https://vocab.design/dock-magnification.md): Scaling each item in a row by how close the pointer is to it, so the item under the cursor swells, its neighbours ramp down, and the row reads as bulging.
- [Dolly and zoom](https://vocab.design/dolly-zoom.md): Borrowing the camera's vocabulary: dolly moves the viewer through the scene, zoom scales the scene itself, and the interface reads as travelling rather than rearranging.
- [Duration](https://vocab.design/duration.md): How long a transition takes from start to finish, measured separately from the shape of its easing.
- [Easing](https://vocab.design/easing.md): The rate of change across an animation, deciding how it accelerates and settles rather than how long it takes.
- [Entrance animation](https://vocab.design/entrance-animation.md): The motion an element plays as it arrives, running from a starting style that only exists before the element was ever rendered.
- [Exit animation](https://vocab.design/exit-animation.md): The motion an element plays on its way out, which requires deferring its removal from the layout until the animation has finished.
- [Fade](https://vocab.design/fade.md): A change in opacity used to bring an element in or take it out, the cheapest transition and the one that implies no spatial relationship.
- [Fade through](https://vocab.design/fade-through.md): Material's transition for unrelated views: the outgoing view fades out completely before the incoming one fades in while scaling up slightly.
- [Fill mode](https://vocab.design/fill-mode.md): Whether an animation's first or last keyframe styles apply outside its running window, which decides if an element snaps back when it finishes or stays where it landed.
- [FLIP](https://vocab.design/flip-animation.md): A technique that measures an element's first and last positions, inverts the difference with a transform, then plays it off, so layout changes animate cheaply.
- [Float animation](https://vocab.design/float-animation.md): A slow continuous up and down drift on an idle element, so a static composition keeps breathing without asking for attention.
- [Follow-through](https://vocab.design/follow-through.md): Parts of a composition that keep moving briefly after the main element stops, and start slightly after it starts, so a group does not move as one rigid block.
- [Frame rate](https://vocab.design/frame-rate.md): How many frames a second the interface actually draws, the budget every animation spends: 60fps leaves about 16ms per frame and a 120Hz display halves it.
- [Gooey effect](https://vocab.design/gooey-effect.md): Blurring a group of shapes and then crushing the blur back to a hard edge so overlapping elements merge into one liquid silhouette as they move apart and together.
- [Height animation](https://vocab.design/height-animation.md): Animating a container between collapsed and its content's natural size, long impossible because height auto did not interpolate and now opened up by interpolate-size and calc-size().
- [Hover lift](https://vocab.design/hover-lift.md): A card or button that rises a few pixels and deepens its shadow while the pointer is over it, so the whole surface reads as lifted toward the reader.
- [Icon morph](https://vocab.design/icon-morph.md): An icon that animates between two meanings rather than cutting, such as a hamburger whose bars rotate into a close cross.
- [Interactive transition](https://vocab.design/interactive-transition.md): A transition whose progress is held by an ongoing gesture, so the reader can drag it partway, hesitate, and either complete it or send it back.
- [Interpolation](https://vocab.design/interpolation.md): The rule that produces the intermediate values between two endpoints, which is why some properties can animate smoothly and others can only switch.
- [Interruptible animation](https://vocab.design/interruptible-animation.md): Motion that can be caught, reversed, or redirected mid-flight from its current value, instead of finishing before it will accept a new input.
- [Jank](https://vocab.design/jank.md): Visible stutter in motion caused by frames arriving late or not at all, so an animation that should be continuous reads as juddering.
- [Jiggle mode](https://vocab.design/jiggle-mode.md): An editing state announced by making every rearrangeable item wobble in place, so the whole screen says it can be reordered.
- [Ken Burns effect](https://vocab.design/ken-burns-effect.md): A slow pan and zoom across a still image that gives it motion, named after the documentary filmmaker who made the technique famous.
- [Keyframe](https://vocab.design/keyframe.md): A point in an animation where a value is pinned, with the frames between generated by interpolating from one pinned point to the next.
- [Layout thrashing](https://vocab.design/layout-thrashing.md): Reading a geometric value after writing to the DOM in the same frame, forcing the browser to lay out synchronously over and over and stalling the animation that caused it.
- [Line drawing animation](https://vocab.design/line-drawing-animation.md): An SVG stroke that appears to draw itself by animating its dash offset along its own length, used for signatures, check marks and illustrated line art.
- [linear() easing](https://vocab.design/linear-easing.md): An easing written as a list of sampled stops rather than a curve, which lets CSS express springs and bounces that no cubic bezier can describe.
- [Lottie](https://vocab.design/lottie.md): A JSON format for vector animations exported from design tools and played natively on the web and mobile, so complex motion ships without video.
- [Magnetic button](https://vocab.design/magnetic-button.md): A control that leans toward the cursor as it approaches, translating a fraction of the distance to its centre so it reads as attracted rather than merely hovered.
- [Marching ants](https://vocab.design/marching-ants.md): The animated dashed outline that circles a selection, moving continuously so the boundary reads as active rather than drawn.
- [Marquee](https://vocab.design/marquee.md): Text or logos that scroll continuously across a strip, either as a decorative ticker or because a label is too long for its box.
- [Modal presentation](https://vocab.design/modal-presentation.md): The slide-up-over transition that puts a sheet or dialog in front of the current screen while what is behind recedes, the platform motion for entering a modal context.
- [Morph transition](https://vocab.design/morph-transition.md): A transition where a shape or icon is interpolated into a different shape rather than swapped, so the two states read as one object changing.
- [Motion blur](https://vocab.design/motion-blur.md): Blurring an element along its direction of travel so fast movement reads as speed instead of teleporting, borrowed from film and rare but real in interfaces.
- [Motion choreography](https://vocab.design/choreography.md): The plan for how several animating elements relate in time and space, deciding what leads, what follows, and what stays still.
- [Motion path](https://vocab.design/motion-path.md): A defined path an element travels along, with its distance and rotation along that path animated instead of its x and y positions.
- [Motion token](https://vocab.design/motion-token.md): A named duration or easing value published by a design system, so timings are chosen from a set rather than typed per component.
- [Orbit animation](https://vocab.design/orbit-animation.md): One element circling another on a continuous path, used for logo constellations and loading states where the revolving is the ornament.
- [Origin-aware animation](https://vocab.design/origin-aware-animation.md): Scaling or fading a panel out of the control that opened it by putting its transform origin on that anchor, so the panel reads as belonging to its trigger.
- [Overshoot](https://vocab.design/overshoot.md): The part of a motion that carries past its final value before coming back, the visual signature of an underdamped spring or a back easing curve.
- [Page curl](https://vocab.design/page-curl.md): A page turn that lifts and bends the leaf away from the spine as the finger drags it, the most literal transition a reader can be given.
- [Page transition](https://vocab.design/page-transition.md): Motion that covers a navigation between two whole pages or routes, replacing the hard cut a document load would otherwise produce.
- [Parallax](https://vocab.design/parallax.md): Moving layers at different rates against the same input, so the slower layers read as farther away and the scene gains depth.
- [Parenting](https://vocab.design/parenting.md): Tying one element's motion to another's so moving or scaling the parent carries the child with it, which is how a group of parts reads as one object instead of several.
- [Particle background](https://vocab.design/particle-background.md): An ambient decorative background of many small moving agents: drifting dots, linked constellations, flocks, or starfields animating behind the page content.
- [Perceptual duration](https://vocab.design/perceptual-duration.md): How long a spring appears to take, measured to the point the movement stops being visible rather than to its mathematical rest, the figure to quote against a timed animation.
- [Pop in](https://vocab.design/pop-in.md): An entrance that scales slightly past full size before settling, so the element arrives with a small snap instead of simply being there.
- [Predictive back](https://vocab.design/predictive-back.md): A back gesture that reveals the destination underneath while the finger is still down, so the swipe can be finished or abandoned once the reader has seen where it goes.
- [Pulse](https://vocab.design/pulse-animation.md): A slow repeating change in scale or opacity that keeps an element alive without moving it, used for waiting states and gentle attention.
- [Push transition](https://vocab.design/push-transition.md): A navigation transition where the new view slides in and pushes the old one off, and reversing it pops back, encoding depth in a stack.
- [Reveal animation](https://vocab.design/reveal-animation.md): Motion that uncovers content already in place, usually by growing a clip or mask outward from a point rather than moving the content itself.
- [Ripple](https://vocab.design/ripple.md): A circular wash that spreads from the point of contact to acknowledge a touch, Material's way of tying feedback to where the finger landed.
- [Scroll pinning](https://vocab.design/scroll-pinning.md): Holding a section fixed in place while the page keeps scrolling, spending scroll distance on an animation instead of on movement.
- [Scroll-linked animation](https://vocab.design/scroll-linked-animation.md): An animation whose progress is bound to scroll position rather than to time, so scrolling back rewinds it exactly.
- [Scroll-triggered animation](https://vocab.design/scroll-triggered-animation.md): An animation that scroll position only starts, after which it runs on its own clock and does not rewind when the reader scrolls back up.
- [Shake](https://vocab.design/shake-animation.md): A short lateral wobble used to reject an input, borrowed from the head shake and read as no rather than as an error message.
- [Shared axis](https://vocab.design/shared-axis.md): Material's transition where outgoing and incoming views slide and fade along the same x, y, or z axis, so direction encodes the navigational relationship.
- [Shimmer](https://vocab.design/shimmer.md): The moving highlight that sweeps across placeholder shapes to signal that content is still on its way.
- [Slide transition](https://vocab.design/slide-transition.md): A transition where content translates in or out along one axis, using direction to say whether the user moved forward, back, up, or down.
- [Sliding indicator](https://vocab.design/sliding-indicator.md): A single underline or pill that travels between tabs to mark the selection instead of each tab drawing its own, so the move itself says which way the selection went.
- [Smooth scrolling](https://vocab.design/smooth-scrolling.md): Animating a programmatic jump so the page travels to its destination instead of cutting there, which keeps an anchor link or a back-to-top button from losing the reader's place.
- [Split-flap animation](https://vocab.design/split-flap-animation.md): A digit or letter changing by flipping through every character between the old value and the new one, imitating the mechanical boards of airports and flip clocks.
- [Spotlight hover](https://vocab.design/spotlight-hover.md): A soft radial glow centred on the pointer's position inside a card, lighting its surface and border as the cursor moves and going dark when the cursor leaves.
- [Spring animation](https://vocab.design/spring-animation.md): Motion driven by a simulated spring (mass, stiffness, damping) instead of a fixed duration, so the element settles rather than stopping on a schedule.
- [Squash and stretch](https://vocab.design/squash-and-stretch.md): Deforming an element along its direction of travel so it reads as having mass and flexibility, usually as a press squash or a launch stretch.
- [Stacking cards](https://vocab.design/stacking-cards.md): A run of sections that each stick at the top of the viewport as the next one slides over it, so scrolling deals the page like a deck rather than passing it by.
- [Stagger](https://vocab.design/stagger.md): Playing the same animation on a set of elements with a small delay added item by item, so the group arrives as a cascade instead of a block.
- [Stepped animation](https://vocab.design/stepped-animation.md): Motion that jumps between a fixed number of discrete positions instead of interpolating, the mechanic behind sprite sheets, ticking clock hands and segmented spinners.
- [Tween](https://vocab.design/tween.md): A single animation from one value to another over a duration, named for the in-between frames a computer fills in.
- [Typewriter effect](https://vocab.design/typewriter-effect.md): Revealing text one character at a time, as if it were being typed, usually with a blinking caret trailing the last letter.
- [Velocity skew](https://vocab.design/velocity-skew.md): Skewing or stretching content in proportion to how fast the page is scrolling and easing it back to square when the scroll stops, so speed shows up in the shape of the content.
- [View progress timeline](https://vocab.design/view-progress-timeline.md): A scroll timeline measured by one element's passage through the scrollport, with named ranges for entering, being contained, covering, and exiting.
- [View transition](https://vocab.design/view-transition.md): An animated change between two states of a page, where the browser photographs before and after and interpolates the elements the two have in common.
- [Wipe](https://vocab.design/wipe.md): A transition where a moving edge or mask travels across the frame, replacing what was there with what comes next.
- [Yellow fade technique](https://vocab.design/yellow-fade-technique.md): Washing a just-changed element in colour and letting it fade back out, so a change made without a page reload is still noticed where it happened.
- [Yo-yo loop](https://vocab.design/yoyo-loop.md): A repeating animation that plays forward then backward instead of jumping back to the start, so a loop has no visible seam.
- [Zoom transition](https://vocab.design/zoom-transition.md): A presentation that scales a tapped element up into the full view it opens, so the destination appears to come from the thing that was touched.

## typography

- [Abbreviation](https://vocab.design/abbreviation.md): A shortened form of a word or phrase, from Dr. to NASA, with its own typographic conventions and an expansion assistive tech can speak.
- [All caps](https://vocab.design/all-caps.md): Text set entirely in capitals, which reads slower than mixed case because the word's outline shape disappears.
- [Aperture](https://vocab.design/aperture.md): The partly enclosed opening in a letter, such as the gap where the two terminals of a c stop or the mouth at the bottom of an e.
- [Ascender](https://vocab.design/ascender.md): The part of a lowercase letter such as b, d, or h that rises above the x-height.
- [Baseline](https://vocab.design/baseline.md): The invisible line that most letters sit on, and the line every other vertical type metric is measured from.
- [Bidirectional text](https://vocab.design/bidirectional-text.md): Text mixing a right-to-left script with left-to-right runs such as numbers or Latin words, where each run keeps its own direction.
- [Blockquote](https://vocab.design/blockquote.md): A passage quoted from another source and set off from the running text as its own block, carrying the attribution with it.
- [Cap height](https://vocab.design/cap-height.md): The height of a capital letter measured from the baseline, and the edge designers usually mean when they say text should line up flush.
- [Ch unit](https://vocab.design/ch-unit.md): A CSS length equal to the advance width of the digit zero in the current font, used to set column widths in characters rather than pixels.
- [Color font](https://vocab.design/color-font.md): A font whose glyphs carry their own colors, gradients, or layers, with a palette the page can override rather than a single ink.
- [Contextual alternates](https://vocab.design/contextual-alternates.md): Substitute letterforms a font swaps in automatically based on the neighbouring characters, so joins and repeats look natural.
- [Counter](https://vocab.design/counter.md): The fully enclosed white space inside a letterform, the ring of an o or the bowl of a b: letter anatomy, not a character count or a CSS counter.
- [Deck](https://vocab.design/deck.md): The short summary line set between a headline and the body, larger than body text and written to sell the article.
- [Descender](https://vocab.design/descender.md): The part of a letter such as g, j, p, or y that drops below the baseline.
- [Drop cap](https://vocab.design/drop-cap.md): An oversized opening letter set into the first lines of a paragraph, marking where the reading starts.
- [Dynamic Type](https://vocab.design/dynamic-type.md): A platform feature that scales interface text to a size the reader chose in system settings, with layouts expected to reflow around it.
- [Em](https://vocab.design/em-unit.md): A relative unit equal to the current font size, historically the width of the square the letter m was cast on.
- [Em dash](https://vocab.design/em-dash.md): The longest common dash, about the width of the letter m, used to set off an abrupt break or an aside inside a sentence.
- [Emoji presentation](https://vocab.design/emoji-presentation.md): Whether a character that can be either a symbol or an emoji renders as flat text or as a colour emoji, selected by a variation selector or by CSS.
- [En dash](https://vocab.design/en-dash.md): A dash about the width of the letter n, used for ranges of numbers and for connections between two things.
- [Eyebrow](https://vocab.design/eyebrow.md): A short line of text above a heading that says what category or series the content belongs to.
- [Fallback font](https://vocab.design/fallback-font.md): The typeface actually used when the preferred one is missing or has not loaded, either for the whole run of text or for characters it lacks.
- [Faux bold](https://vocab.design/faux-bold.md): A bold or italic the browser fakes by smearing or shearing the regular weight, because the real style was never loaded.
- [Fine print](https://vocab.design/fine-print.md): Qualifying text set small and set last, carrying the conditions that the larger claim above it leaves out.
- [First-line indent](https://vocab.design/first-line-indent.md): Indenting the opening line of a paragraph so the start of each paragraph is visible without a blank line between them.
- [Fluid typography](https://vocab.design/fluid-typography.md): Type sizes that scale continuously with the viewport between a minimum and a maximum, rather than jumping at breakpoints.
- [FOFT](https://vocab.design/foft.md): A loading strategy that shows the roman weight as soon as it arrives and lets the remaining styles swap in afterwards, so the swap happens in stages.
- [FOIT](https://vocab.design/foit.md): The blank period when a browser hides text entirely rather than show it in a fallback face while the web font loads.
- [Font metric override](https://vocab.design/font-metric-override.md): Reshaping a fallback font's size and vertical metrics in CSS so it occupies the same space as the web font and the swap shifts nothing.
- [Font pairing](https://vocab.design/font-pairing.md): Choosing two or more typefaces that work together, usually one expressive and one neutral, with enough contrast to read as a deliberate choice.
- [Font smoothing](https://vocab.design/font-smoothing.md): How a device softens the edges of letterforms, either by shading whole pixels grey or by lighting a pixel's colored subpixels separately.
- [Font stack](https://vocab.design/font-stack.md): The ordered list of typefaces a rule names, each tried in turn until one is available, ending in a generic family.
- [Font subsetting](https://vocab.design/font-subsetting.md): Shipping only the characters a page actually needs, cutting the font file down and letting the browser fetch ranges on demand.
- [Font weight](https://vocab.design/font-weight.md): How thick a typeface's strokes are, named in steps from thin to black and numbered from 100 to 900 on the web.
- [FOUT](https://vocab.design/fout.md): The visible swap when a page first paints text in a fallback face and then re-renders it once the web font arrives.
- [Glyph](https://vocab.design/glyph.md): A single drawn shape in a font, which may be one character, a variant of one, or several characters fused together.
- [Grade](https://vocab.design/grade-axis.md): A variable font axis that thickens or thins strokes without changing any character's width, so text can get darker without reflowing.
- [Half-leading](https://vocab.design/half-leading.md): The empty space a browser splits evenly above and below a line of text when line height exceeds the font's own height, which is why text boxes never sit flush.
- [Hanging indent](https://vocab.design/hanging-indent.md): A paragraph whose first line starts further left than the rest, so the following lines are indented under it.
- [Hanging punctuation](https://vocab.design/hanging-punctuation.md): Letting quotes, hyphens, and other light marks sit outside the text column so the edge of the text reads as straight to the eye.
- [Heading](https://vocab.design/heading.md): A short line of type that names the section under it and, by its size and weight, says how far down the outline that section sits.
- [Hinting](https://vocab.design/font-hinting.md): Instructions inside a font that nudge its outlines onto the pixel grid at small sizes so stems stay crisp and even.
- [Hyphenation](https://vocab.design/hyphenation.md): Breaking a word across two lines at a syllable boundary so lines fill more evenly, marked with a hyphen at the break.
- [Hyphenation ladder](https://vocab.design/hyphenation-ladder.md): Three or more consecutive lines ending in a hyphen, which builds a visible staircase down the right edge of a column.
- [Icon font](https://vocab.design/icon-font.md): A font whose glyphs are icons rather than letters, addressed by code point or by a ligature so an icon can be styled like text.
- [Ink trap](https://vocab.design/ink-trap.md): A notch cut out of a letter's inside corners so spreading ink or blurring pixels do not fill the joint solid.
- [Italic](https://vocab.design/italic.md): A companion style with letterforms redrawn on a cursive model, not merely slanted, used for emphasis and titles.
- [Justified text](https://vocab.design/justified-text.md): Text set so both edges of the column are flush, achieved by stretching or squeezing the spaces between words on each line.
- [Kerning](https://vocab.design/kerning.md): The adjustment of space between two particular letters so the pair reads evenly.
- [Kinetic typography](https://vocab.design/kinetic-typography.md): Type animated over time, where letters and words move, scale, stagger, or morph so the setting carries tone and emphasis a static line cannot.
- [Leading](https://vocab.design/leading.md): The vertical distance from one baseline of type to the next, which sets how a paragraph holds together as a block.
- [Legibility](https://vocab.design/legibility.md): How easily one letter can be told apart from another, a property of the typeface's drawing rather than of how the text is set.
- [Ligature](https://vocab.design/ligature.md): A single glyph that replaces two or more letters whose shapes would otherwise collide, such as the f and i pair.
- [Line clamp](https://vocab.design/line-clamp.md): Cutting a block of text off after a fixed number of lines, with an ellipsis at the end of the last one.
- [Lining figures](https://vocab.design/lining-figures.md): Numerals all drawn to cap height so they line up evenly with capitals and with each other.
- [Lorem ipsum](https://vocab.design/lorem-ipsum.md): Scrambled pseudo-Latin placeholder text used so a layout can be judged on its shape and texture before the real copy exists.
- [Measure](https://vocab.design/measure.md): The width of a column of text, judged in characters per line, with roughly 45 to 75 treated as the comfortable range for reading.
- [Modular scale](https://vocab.design/modular-scale.md): A type scale generated by multiplying a base size by a fixed ratio, so every step is proportionally related to the one before it.
- [Monospace](https://vocab.design/monospace.md): A typeface in which every character occupies the same horizontal width, so characters stack into columns down the page.
- [Named instance](https://vocab.design/named-instance.md): A specific point in a variable font's design space that the designer has given a style name, so it can be picked like an ordinary weight.
- [Non-breaking space](https://vocab.design/non-breaking-space.md): A space that renders normally but forbids a line break, gluing two words together so they never end up on separate lines.
- [Oblique](https://vocab.design/oblique.md): An upright typeface slanted to the right without redrawing its letters, which is why it lacks the cursive forms a true italic has.
- [Oldstyle figures](https://vocab.design/oldstyle-figures.md): Numerals with varying heights, some rising and some dropping below the baseline, so numbers blend into lowercase running text.
- [OpenType features](https://vocab.design/opentype-features.md): Optional glyph substitutions and spacing rules packed inside a font file, addressed by four-letter tags and switched on from CSS.
- [Optical kerning](https://vocab.design/optical-kerning.md): Letting software space letter pairs by looking at their shapes, instead of using the pair values the type designer built into the font.
- [Optical size](https://vocab.design/optical-size.md): A font adjusting its own drawing for the size it is set at, thickening strokes and opening spacing for small text and refining both for large.
- [Orphan](https://vocab.design/orphan.md): A first line of a paragraph left alone at the bottom of a column or page, with the rest of the paragraph carried over.
- [Oversized typography](https://vocab.design/oversized-typography.md): Type set far past reading size so the words carry the layout, the headline doing the work a photograph would otherwise be hired for.
- [Pangram](https://vocab.design/pangram.md): A sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet at least once, used to show a whole character set in one line.
- [Petite caps](https://vocab.design/petite-caps.md): Capitals drawn to exactly x-height, shorter than small caps, so they sit flush with the lowercase around them.
- [Pilcrow](https://vocab.design/pilcrow.md): The paragraph mark, a reversed P with a doubled stem, used to show where a paragraph begins or as a hover anchor beside a heading.
