- [Point size](https://vocab.design/point-size.md): The nominal size of type, measured in points, which describes the body the letters are drawn on rather than the height of any letter.
- [Prime mark](https://vocab.design/prime-mark.md): The slanted tick used for feet, inches, minutes, and seconds, which is a different character from either a straight quote or a curly one.
- [Pull quote](https://vocab.design/pull-quote.md): A phrase lifted out of an article and set large as a graphic element, to draw a browsing reader into the text.
- [Rag](https://vocab.design/rag.md): The uneven edge left by unjustified text, and the thing typographers tune so that edge makes no distracting shapes down the side of a paragraph.
- [Raised cap](https://vocab.design/raised-cap.md): An oversized opening letter that sits on the first line's baseline and rises above the text, rather than sinking into it.
- [Readability](https://vocab.design/readability.md): How comfortably a body of text can be read at length, a property of the setting: size, measure, leading, and contrast.
- [River](https://vocab.design/river.md): An accidental channel of white space running down a paragraph where word spaces on consecutive lines happen to line up.
- [Ruby annotation](https://vocab.design/ruby-annotation.md): Small guide text set beside or above a run of base text, most often to give the pronunciation of East Asian characters.
- [Runt](https://vocab.design/runt.md): A single word left alone on the last line of a paragraph or heading.
- [Sans-serif](https://vocab.design/sans-serif.md): A typeface drawn without finishing strokes on the ends of its stems, which is the default register of most interface type.
- [Sentence case](https://vocab.design/sentence-case.md): Capitalising only the first word of a label or heading, plus any proper nouns, as you would in an ordinary sentence.
- [Serif](https://vocab.design/serif.md): The small finishing stroke at the end of a letter's stem, and by extension the class of typefaces that have them.
- [Signed distance field](https://vocab.design/signed-distance-field.md): A texture storing each pixel's distance to a shape's edge rather than its color, so glyphs and icons rendered from it stay crisp at any scale on the GPU.
- [Small caps](https://vocab.design/small-caps.md): Capital letters drawn at roughly lowercase height, with weight adjusted to match, so an abbreviation does not shout inside running text.
- [Smart quotes](https://vocab.design/smart-quotes.md): The curved opening and closing quotation marks a typeface actually draws, as opposed to the straight vertical marks inherited from typewriters.
- [Soft hyphen](https://vocab.design/soft-hyphen.md): An invisible character placed inside a word that marks where a hyphen may appear if the word has to break, and stays hidden otherwise.
- [Strikethrough](https://vocab.design/strikethrough.md): A rule drawn through the middle of text to mark it as removed, superseded, or no longer the current price.
- [Stylistic set](https://vocab.design/stylistic-set.md): A numbered bundle of alternate glyphs inside a font, switched on as a group to change the look of certain letters.
- [Superfamily](https://vocab.design/superfamily.md): A type system whose serif, sans, and sometimes mono members share one skeleton, so they pair by construction rather than by taste.
- [Superscript](https://vocab.design/superscript.md): Small raised characters used for footnote markers, ordinals, and exponents, ideally drawn by the font rather than shrunk by software.
- [Swash](https://vocab.design/swash.md): A letter drawn with an ornamental flourish, usually an extended entry or exit stroke on an italic capital.
- [System font](https://vocab.design/system-font.md): The typeface the operating system uses for its own interface, requested by keyword so each platform supplies its native face.
- [Tabular figures](https://vocab.design/tabular-figures.md): Numerals drawn to identical widths so digits stack into columns, and so a changing number does not shift the text around it.
- [Text balancing](https://vocab.design/text-balancing.md): Choosing line breaks so a short block of text has lines of roughly equal length instead of a long first line and a stub second one.
- [Text box trim](https://vocab.design/text-box-trim.md): Cutting the leftover space above and below a line of text so the box hugs the cap height and baseline instead of the font's full ascent and descent.
- [Title case](https://vocab.design/title-case.md): Capitalising the first letter of each significant word in a heading or label, leaving short articles, conjunctions and prepositions lowercase.
- [Tittle](https://vocab.design/tittle.md): The dot above a lowercase i or j.
- [Tofu](https://vocab.design/tofu.md): The empty rectangle a font renders when it has no glyph for a character, named for the block of bean curd it resembles.
- [Tracking](https://vocab.design/tracking.md): The uniform space added to or removed from every letter across a run of text.
- [Truncation](https://vocab.design/truncation.md): Cutting text that does not fit and marking the cut, usually with an ellipsis, so the reader knows something was removed.
- [Type scale](https://vocab.design/type-scale.md): The fixed set of text sizes a design allows, chosen so sizes relate to each other rather than being picked one at a time.
- [Type specimen](https://vocab.design/type-specimen.md): A display of a typeface's characters, sizes, and styles made to show what the face can do rather than to communicate the text itself.
- [Typeface](https://vocab.design/typeface.md): The designed set of letterforms itself, as distinct from a font, which is one particular file or instance you actually use.
- [Typographic color](https://vocab.design/typographic-color.md): The overall lightness or darkness a block of text produces when you stop reading it and look at it as a grey texture.
- [Typographic hierarchy](https://vocab.design/typographic-hierarchy.md): The ordering of text by visual weight so a reader can tell at a glance what is a title, what is body, and what is a caption.
- [Typography token](https://vocab.design/typography-token.md): A named bundle of type values (family, size, weight, line height, tracking) that a design system hands out instead of raw numbers.
- [Underline](https://vocab.design/underline.md): A rule drawn under text, on the web the default marker for a link, ideally set to skip the descenders it would otherwise cross.
- [Variable font](https://vocab.design/variable-font.md): One font file that contains a continuous design space, so any weight, width, or other axis value between the extremes can be requested.
- [Variation axis](https://vocab.design/variation-axis.md): One dimension a variable font can move along, named by a four-letter tag: lowercase for the five registered axes, uppercase for custom ones.
- [Vertical rhythm](https://vocab.design/vertical-rhythm.md): Spacing every block of text by multiples of one line height so the page keeps an even beat from top to bottom.
- [Vertical writing mode](https://vocab.design/vertical-writing-mode.md): Setting lines to run top to bottom in columns rather than left to right, as traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean typography does.
- [Web font](https://vocab.design/web-font.md): A font file downloaded by the page rather than taken from the reader's device, declared in CSS and delivered like any other asset.
- [Widow](https://vocab.design/widow.md): A short last line of a paragraph, often a single word, stranded at the top of the next column or page.
- [Word break](https://vocab.design/word-break.md): Whether a long unbroken string is allowed to split mid-word rather than overflow its container, and where that split may happen.
- [Word spacing](https://vocab.design/word-spacing.md): The width of the gaps between words, which justification stretches and which, set too wide, opens rivers down a paragraph.
- [X-height](https://vocab.design/x-height.md): The height of a lowercase x in a typeface, measured from the baseline, which is what makes two fonts at the same point size look different sizes.
- [Zero-width space](https://vocab.design/zero-width-space.md): An invisible character that takes no width and adds a legal break point, letting a long string wrap without showing a hyphen.

## color

- [60-30-10 rule](https://vocab.design/sixty-thirty-ten-rule.md): A proportion guideline that gives about 60 percent of a layout to a dominant colour, 30 percent to a secondary, and 10 percent to an accent.
- [Accent color](https://vocab.design/accent-color.md): The one saturated colour an interface spends sparingly on the things it wants clicked, so its rarity is what makes it read as important.
- [Additive colour](https://vocab.design/additive-color.md): Colour made by adding light, where red, green and blue at full strength give white, which is why a screen is at its brightest when it is showing all three.
- [Alpha channel](https://vocab.design/alpha-channel.md): The transparency component carried inside a colour value itself, which lets a border or fill blend with whatever surface it lands on instead of assuming one.
- [Alpha compositing](https://vocab.design/alpha-compositing.md): The arithmetic that combines a translucent layer with what is beneath it, and the reason two stacked 50 percent layers do not add up to fully opaque.
- [Analogous colors](https://vocab.design/analogous-colors.md): A palette built from hues that neighbour each other on the wheel, giving a calm scheme with no colour fighting another for attention.
- [APCA](https://vocab.design/apca.md): A perceptual contrast algorithm proposed for WCAG 3 that scores a text and background pair as an Lc value and takes font size and weight into account.
- [Blend mode](https://vocab.design/blend-mode.md): A formula for combining a layer's colour with the colour behind it, such as multiply or screen or overlay, instead of simply covering it.
- [Brand color](https://vocab.design/brand-color.md): The colour an organisation owns in a customer's memory, carried into a product as the seed for its palette rather than used directly on every surface.
- [Categorical palette](https://vocab.design/categorical-palette.md): A data palette of distinct hues at roughly equal visual weight, used for groups that have no order so no colour reads as larger than another.
- [Chroma](https://vocab.design/chroma.md): Colourfulness measured in absolute terms rather than as a percentage of the maximum, so a light pastel and a dark ink can be compared on one scale.
- [CMYK](https://vocab.design/cmyk.md): The subtractive print colour model: cyan, magenta and yellow inks plus a key black, mixing by absorbing light, with a gamut narrower than any screen's.
- [Color alias](https://vocab.design/color-alias.md): A second name pointing at an existing scale so one palette can answer to several meanings, letting yellow serve as both warning and pending without duplication.
- [Color banding](https://vocab.design/color-banding.md): The visible stripes that appear across a gradient when a display or file cannot render enough intermediate steps to keep the transition smooth.
- [Color coding](https://vocab.design/color-coding.md): Giving each category its own colour so the eye can group and find by hue, which holds only while the set stays small and one colour means one thing everywhere.
- [Color gamut](https://vocab.design/color-gamut.md): The set of colours a space or a display can actually produce, which is why a value that is legal in one notation can be impossible on a given screen.
- [Color harmonization](https://vocab.design/color-harmonization.md): Nudging an outside colour's hue toward the current scheme so a fixed brand or status colour sits inside a generated palette without looking imported.
- [Color harmony](https://vocab.design/color-harmony.md): A rule for choosing colours by their positions on the wheel, such as complementary or analogous or triadic, so a palette holds together by construction.
- [Color interpolation](https://vocab.design/color-interpolation.md): The rule for what happens between two colours in a gradient or transition, including which space the blend runs in and which way around the hue wheel it travels.
- [Color ramp](https://vocab.design/color-ramp.md): One hue rendered at a fixed series of lightness steps, numbered so that the same step means the same job in every hue.
- [Color role](https://vocab.design/color-role.md): A named job in the interface, such as surface or outline or on-primary, that components style themselves against instead of reaching for a palette value.
- [Color scheme](https://vocab.design/color-scheme.md): The declaration that a page or element supports light or dark rendering, which also tells the browser which palette to use for scrollbars and form controls.
- [Color space](https://vocab.design/color-space.md): A coordinate system for describing colour, where the choice of axes decides whether arithmetic like mixing or stepping a ramp matches what the eye sees.
- [Color stop](https://vocab.design/color-stop.md): A colour pinned at a position along a gradient, with an optional hint between two stops that moves the halfway point of the transition off centre.
- [Color temperature](https://vocab.design/color-temperature.md): Whether a colour reads warm (toward red and orange) or cool (toward blue), the axis designers use to bias a neutral grey without changing its lightness.
- [Color theme](https://vocab.design/color-theme.md): A complete named set of colour values a product can swap in whole, so light, dark, high contrast and per-tenant branding are the same mechanism.
- [Color token](https://vocab.design/color-token.md): A named colour decision stored once and referenced everywhere, so retheming is a change to the value rather than an edit at every place it is used.
- [Color wheel](https://vocab.design/color-wheel.md): A circular arrangement of hues that makes relationships between colours geometric, so a scheme becomes a shape drawn across the circle.
- [color-mix()](https://vocab.design/color-mix.md): A CSS function that blends two colours by a chosen percentage in a chosen colour space, so hover and disabled variants are derived rather than hand-picked.
- [Complementary colors](https://vocab.design/complementary-colors.md): Two hues sitting opposite each other on the colour wheel, the pairing that produces the strongest contrast and the loudest accent.
- [Conic gradient](https://vocab.design/conic-gradient.md): A gradient whose colours sweep around a centre point like a clock hand rather than along a line, the shape behind pie charts, colour wheels and progress rings.
- [Container color](https://vocab.design/container-color.md): A muted companion to an accent, light enough to fill a chip or a card behind ordinary text, so an accent can shade a region without shouting.
- [Contrast ratio](https://vocab.design/contrast-ratio.md): A number from 1:1 to 21:1 describing how far apart two colours sit in relative luminance, used to decide whether text on a background is readable.
- [currentColor](https://vocab.design/currentcolor.md): A CSS keyword meaning the element's own text colour, letting borders, icons and fills inherit whatever colour the surrounding text happens to be.
- [Dark mode](https://vocab.design/dark-mode.md): A second palette built on dark surfaces with light foregrounds, derived from the light one by rebalancing lightness and saturation rather than by inverting it.
- [Dithering](https://vocab.design/dithering.md): Adding fine noise to a gradient or image so the eye averages neighbouring pixels into the missing intermediate colours, hiding the bands.
- [Diverging palette](https://vocab.design/diverging-palette.md): A data palette built from two sequential scales meeting at a neutral midpoint, used when values run above and below a meaningful zero.
- [Duotone](https://vocab.design/duotone.md): An image rendered in two colours instead of full colour, mapping its shadows to one hue and its highlights to another so photography joins the brand palette.
- [Elevation overlay](https://vocab.design/elevation-overlay.md): The older dark theme technique of laying white over a surface at an opacity that rises with elevation, because shadows are nearly invisible on dark backgrounds.
- [Emphasis level](https://vocab.design/emphasis-level.md): A three-rung text hierarchy, high, medium and disabled, ranked by stepping the opacity of one foreground colour instead of naming a separate colour for each rung.
- [Flash of inaccurate color theme](https://vocab.design/flash-of-inaccurate-color-theme.md): The moment a page paints in the wrong theme before the stored preference is applied, showing a light flash to a reader who chose dark.
- [Forced colors mode](https://vocab.design/forced-colors-mode.md): An operating system mode that replaces a page's palette with a small user-chosen set of system colours, overriding almost everything an author specified.
- [Gamut mapping](https://vocab.design/gamut-mapping.md): Converting a colour that falls outside a display's range into the nearest one inside it, usually by lowering chroma in OKLCH rather than clipping each channel.
- [Gradient](https://vocab.design/gradient.md): A fill that transitions between two or more colours across a shape, defined by colour stops and by the space the transition is interpolated in.
- [HCT](https://vocab.design/hct.md): Material's colour space of hue, chroma and tone, which borrows hue and chroma from CAM16 and lightness from CIELAB so tone alone predicts contrast.
- [Hex color](https://vocab.design/hex-color.md): A colour written as a hash followed by three, four, six or eight hexadecimal digits, the notation most handoffs still speak even when the source is OKLCH.
- [Hue](https://vocab.design/hue.md): The attribute that gives a colour its name, red or teal or violet, expressed as an angle around a colour wheel independent of how light or vivid it is.
- [Hue shift](https://vocab.design/hue-shift.md): Rotating hue deliberately along a ramp, warmer at the light end and cooler at the dark end, so a scale looks alive instead of like one colour fading out.
- [Interaction color step](https://vocab.design/interaction-color-step.md): The convention that hover, active and selected are the next steps along the same scale rather than separate colours, so states are derived from one ramp.
- [Inverse color](https://vocab.design/inverse-color.md): A surface and text pair deliberately flipped against the current theme, so a snackbar or tooltip reads as a foreign object that arrived from outside the page.
- [light-dark()](https://vocab.design/light-dark.md): A CSS function that takes two colours and returns the one matching the page's current colour scheme, collapsing a theme's light and dark values into one declaration.
- [Lightness](https://vocab.design/lightness.md): How light or dark a colour reads, from black at one end to white at the other, held separately from its hue and its colourfulness.
- [Mesh gradient](https://vocab.design/mesh-gradient.md): A soft multi-point blend built from colours placed on a grid and smoothed between them, giving the blurred, cloudlike backgrounds a linear gradient cannot.
- [Monochromatic palette](https://vocab.design/monochromatic-palette.md): A scheme drawn from one hue at many lightness and saturation levels, so hierarchy comes from contrast alone rather than from colour difference.
- [Named color](https://vocab.design/named-color.md): One of the CSS keywords such as tomato or rebeccapurple that map to fixed sRGB values, a fossil vocabulary still useful for prototypes and debugging.
- [Neutral palette](https://vocab.design/neutral-palette.md): The greys an interface is mostly made of, ramped from page background to body text, which carry the structure while the accent carries the attention.
- [OKLCH](https://vocab.design/oklch.md): A colour notation of lightness, chroma and hue built on Oklab, where changing the hue leaves the perceived lightness alone and equal steps look equal.
- [On-color](https://vocab.design/on-color.md): A colour defined by what it sits on, such as on-primary or on-surface, so every fill ships with the foreground guaranteed to be readable against it.
- [Opacity](https://vocab.design/opacity.md): How much of what is behind an element shows through it, applied to the whole element and its children at once rather than to a single colour value.
- [Outline color](https://vocab.design/outline-color.md): The role that draws boundaries, split into a stronger value for edges that must be seen and a weaker one for dividers that only need to hint at structure.
- [Perceptual uniformity](https://vocab.design/perceptual-uniformity.md): The property of a colour space where equal numeric distances look like equal visual differences, which is what makes a generated ramp step evenly.
- [Primitive color token](https://vocab.design/primitive-color-token.md): A raw palette value named for what it is, like blue-500, sitting under the semantic layer that names colours for what they do.
- [Relative color syntax](https://vocab.design/relative-color-syntax.md): CSS notation that builds a new colour from an existing one by naming an origin colour with from and then adjusting individual channels.
- [Relative luminance](https://vocab.design/relative-luminance.md): The brightness of a colour measured on a 0 to 1 scale after each channel is linearised, which is the input every WCAG contrast calculation actually uses.
- [Saturation](https://vocab.design/saturation.md): How far a colour is from grey on a scale where 100 percent is the pure hue and 0 percent is neutral, as modelled by HSL and its relatives.
- [Scrim](https://vocab.design/scrim.md): A translucent or gradient layer laid over imagery or behind a dialog, dimming what is beneath so text on top clears contrast or so focus moves forward.
- [Scrollbar color](https://vocab.design/scrollbar-color.md): The thumb and track colours of a scrollbar, which a page can set explicitly or leave to the declared colour scheme so the browser draws its own dark variant.
- [Seed color](https://vocab.design/seed-color.md): The single input colour an algorithm expands into a whole scheme, so a palette becomes something derived from one decision rather than picked swatch by swatch.
- [Selection color](https://vocab.design/selection-color.md): The highlight painted behind text a reader has selected, which a page can restyle and thereby break the contrast the operating system had guaranteed.
- [Semantic color](https://vocab.design/semantic-color.md): A colour named for the job it does rather than the colour it is, so that "danger" or "surface" can be repointed without renaming anything that uses it.
- [Sequential palette](https://vocab.design/sequential-palette.md): A data palette that runs light to dark in one direction, encoding an ordered quantity so that darker always means more.
- [Shade](https://vocab.design/shade.md): A colour with black mixed in, darker than the original hue and typically used for pressed states, borders and dark theme surfaces.
- [sRGB](https://vocab.design/srgb.md): The default colour space of the web, the one hex codes and plain rgb() values live in, and the baseline every wider gamut is described relative to.
- [State layer](https://vocab.design/state-layer.md): A translucent sheet of the content colour laid over a control at a fixed opacity per state, so hover, focus and pressed are one rule instead of three palettes.
- [Static color](https://vocab.design/static-color.md): A colour deliberately excluded from theming because it sits on something that never changes, such as a label over a photo or a fixed brand mark.
- [Status color](https://vocab.design/status-color.md): The small fixed set of colours a product reserves for outcome, typically success, warning, danger and info, so meaning is consistent wherever it appears.
- [Subtractive colour](https://vocab.design/subtractive-color.md): Colour made by taking light away, where inks stack towards black and every added layer can only darken, which is why a screen blue cannot be printed.
- [Surface color](https://vocab.design/surface-color.md): The colour of a plane that content sits on, defined as a set of stacked levels so a card on a page and a sheet on a card are told apart by value.
- [Surface tint](https://vocab.design/surface-tint.md): A wash of the primary colour blended into a surface in proportion to its elevation, so height reads as a colour shift rather than only as a shadow.
- [Swatch](https://vocab.design/swatch.md): A small block of flat colour shown as a sample, used in pickers and documentation to stand in for a value the reader cannot otherwise see.
- [Syntax highlighting](https://vocab.design/syntax-highlighting.md): Colouring code by what each token is, keyword or string or comment or name, so the structure and the typo are visible before a line has actually been read.
- [System color keyword](https://vocab.design/system-color-keyword.md): A CSS keyword such as Canvas, CanvasText or LinkText that resolves to a colour chosen by the operating system rather than by the page.
- [Tint](https://vocab.design/tint.md): A colour with white mixed in, lighter than the original hue and used for faint fills, hover washes and subtle backgrounds.
- [Tinted neutral](https://vocab.design/tinted-neutral.md): A grey with a trace of the brand hue mixed in, so backgrounds and borders belong to the palette instead of reading as a separate, colder system.
- [Transparency checkerboard](https://vocab.design/transparency-checkerboard.md): The light grey and white checker grid a design tool paints behind transparent regions, a convention so universal that the pattern itself now reads as meaning alpha.
- [Triadic color scheme](https://vocab.design/triadic-colors.md): A palette of three hues spaced evenly around the colour wheel, vivid by construction and usually applied with one hue dominant.
- [True black theme](https://vocab.design/true-black-theme.md): A dark palette whose background is pure black rather than near black, which switches OLED pixels off entirely but makes elements look like they float in a void.
- [Vibrancy](https://vocab.design/vibrancy.md): Apple's treatment where foreground colour is derived from the blurred content behind a material, so labels on a translucent panel shift with whatever they sit over.
- [Wide gamut](https://vocab.design/wide-gamut.md): Colour beyond what sRGB can express, addressed in CSS through spaces such as display-p3 and rec2020 and shown only on displays that reach that far.

## surface

- [Bevel and emboss](https://vocab.design/bevel.md): Light and dark edges drawn along a shape's border so it reads as raised or carved, the depth trick behind classic desktop buttons.
- [Chamfer](https://vocab.design/chamfer.md): A corner cut flat at an angle instead of rounded, the sharp-edged sibling of border-radius that reads industrial, military, or sci-fi.
- [Concentric corner radius](https://vocab.design/concentric-corner-radius.md): Sizing a nested shape's corners so its curve shares a centre with the one outside it, the inner radius being the outer radius less the padding between them.
- [Corner radius](https://vocab.design/corner-radius.md): How far a shape's corners are rounded off, measured as the radius of the circle that replaces the square angle, and the one number that decides how soft a UI reads.
- [Dot grid background](https://vocab.design/dot-grid-background.md): A faint repeating field of dots or ruled squares behind content, borrowed from graph paper and canvas tools to suggest an editable surface rather than a page.
- [Elevation](https://vocab.design/elevation.md): How high a surface sits above the one behind it, expressed as a shadow, a tint, or both, and held to a few named steps so that height means something.
- [Gloss](https://vocab.design/gloss.md): A wet plastic finish made from a light gradient across the top half of a control, a highlight arc, and a darker lower half.
- [Gradient border](https://vocab.design/gradient-border.md): An outline filled with a gradient rather than a single color, usually built from a conic or linear gradient behind a masked shape so the hue travels around the edge.
- [Grainy gradient](https://vocab.design/grainy-gradient.md): A gradient with a fine noise layer over it, added to hide banding and give a flat background the texture of printed paper or film.
- [Halftone](https://vocab.design/halftone.md): Rendering tone as a grid of dots that vary in size, borrowed from print and used to give flat interface art a comic or newsprint feel.
- [Holographic foil](https://vocab.design/holographic-foil.md): A finish that shifts hue with viewing angle, imitating foil, soap film, or a CD surface with banded rainbow gradients over a pale metallic ground.
- [Letterpress text](https://vocab.design/letterpress-text.md): A text effect that fakes stamping into the surface, using a one pixel light shadow below the glyphs and a slightly darker fill above it.
- [Long shadow](https://vocab.design/long-shadow.md): A flat era decoration where an icon casts a single hard shadow at 45 degrees that runs far past the shape before fading out.
- [Neon glow](https://vocab.design/neon-glow.md): A saturated colour surrounded by layered soft shadows of the same hue, so type or a border reads as a lit tube against a dark surface.
- [Organic blob](https://vocab.design/blob-shape.md): A soft irregular shape with no straight edges, used as a background accent or image mask to soften a strictly rectangular layout.
- [Progressive blur](https://vocab.design/progressive-blur.md): A blur whose strength ramps across a region instead of applying evenly, so content fades into softness toward an edge rather than stopping at a hard line.
- [Scanlines](https://vocab.design/scanlines.md): Thin repeating dark lines laid over an interface to imitate the raster of a cathode ray tube screen, often with a slight curve and flicker.
- [Specular highlight](https://vocab.design/specular-highlight.md): The bright reflection drawn on a surface to say it is glossy, placed where a light source would strike a curved object.
- [Squircle](https://vocab.design/squircle.md): A rounded square whose corners curve continuously into the sides instead of meeting a circular arc, the shape behind iOS app icons.
- [Terrazzo](https://vocab.design/terrazzo.md): A background pattern of small irregular chips scattered on a plain field, copied from poured stone flooring and used flat and multicolored behind interface content.
- [Vignette](https://vocab.design/vignette.md): A gradual darkening toward the edges of an image that pulls the eye to the centre, borrowed from lens falloff and applied deliberately for focus and mood.

## accessibility

- [Accessibility annotation](https://vocab.design/accessibility-annotation.md): Notes attached to a design file that spell out the things a mockup cannot show: heading levels, focus order, names, roles, live regions, and alt text.
- [Accessibility grouping](https://vocab.design/accessibility-grouping.md): Collapsing a cluster of elements, an icon plus a label plus a value, into one thing assistive technology stops at, instead of three stops that mean nothing apart.
- [Accessibility overlay](https://vocab.design/accessibility-overlay.md): A third party script bolted onto a site with a promise of automatic compliance, usually a floating widget of font and contrast toggles that fixes nothing underneath.
- [Accessibility trait](https://vocab.design/accessibility-trait.md): The platform flag on a native view that says what it is and how it behaves, the mobile counterpart to a role plus a state, and the thing a custom control has to set by hand.
- [Accessibility tree](https://vocab.design/accessibility-tree.md): The parallel tree a browser derives from the DOM, holding the role, name, state, and value that assistive technology actually reads.
- [Accessible authentication](https://vocab.design/accessible-authentication.md): A sign-in route that never requires a cognitive function test such as recalling a password or solving a puzzle without offering an alternative.
- [Accessible description](https://vocab.design/accessible-description.md): Supplementary text announced after a control's name, carrying hint or error detail without becoming part of the name itself.
- [Accessible name](https://vocab.design/accessible-name.md): The string assistive technology announces for a control, computed from label, aria-labelledby, aria-label, or its own content in a fixed order of precedence.
- [Active descendant](https://vocab.design/active-descendant.md): A focus technique where DOM focus stays on a container or input and aria-activedescendant names which child is active, used when focus must not move.
- [Alt text](https://vocab.design/alt-text.md): The text alternative that stands in for an image, written to serve the same purpose in the same context rather than to describe every detail.
- [ARIA notify](https://vocab.design/aria-notify.md): A proposed API for speaking a message directly to assistive technology, without the live region trick of mutating hidden text and hoping the timing works out.
- [aria-hidden](https://vocab.design/aria-hidden.md): An attribute that removes an element and its whole subtree from the accessibility tree while leaving it visible on screen.
- [Atomic live region](https://vocab.design/atomic-live-region.md): A live region setting that makes assistive technology re-read the whole region when any part of it changes, instead of only the changed fragment.
- [Audio control](https://vocab.design/audio-control.md): A way to stop sound that started on its own, because autoplaying audio drowns out the screen reader voice a reader depends on to find the control that stops it.
- [Audio description](https://vocab.design/audio-description.md): A narration track describing visual information the soundtrack leaves out, fitted into the gaps between dialogue.
- [Braille display](https://vocab.design/braille-display.md): A refreshable braille row that renders the same accessibility tree as speech, with abbreviated role names authors can override.
- [Browse mode](https://vocab.design/browse-mode.md): The screen reader mode that intercepts keystrokes for reading and navigation, as opposed to focus or forms mode where keys reach the page.
- [Busy state](https://vocab.design/busy-state.md): Marking a region as still loading so assistive technology waits for the finished result instead of reading each row as it streams in.
- [Button versus link](https://vocab.design/button-versus-link.md): The rule that decides which element to use: a link goes somewhere, a button does something, and the choice sets the keyboard, the cursor, and the announced role.
- [Captions](https://vocab.design/captions.md): Synchronised text for a video's audio, including speaker changes and meaningful sound, distinct from subtitles which only translate dialogue.
- [Change of context](https://vocab.design/change-of-context.md): A shift big enough to disorient a reader, a new page, a new window, a moved focus, a rearranged form, and the rule that it should follow a request rather than a keystroke.
- [Character key shortcuts](https://vocab.design/character-key-shortcuts.md): Single letter shortcuts that fire without a modifier, which must be switchable off or remappable because speech input and screen readers trigger them by accident.
- [Chart description](https://vocab.design/chart-description.md): The text alternative for a chart: a summary of the takeaway plus access to the underlying values, not a recital of the pixels.
- [Chunking](https://vocab.design/chunking.md): Breaking content into small labelled pieces, short paragraphs, lists, and headings, so a reader can hold one piece at a time instead of the whole wall.
- [Cognitive load](https://vocab.design/cognitive-load.md): The mental effort an interface demands, split between the work the task really needs and the work the design added by way of clutter, jargon, and avoidable steps.
- [Color vision deficiency](https://vocab.design/color-vision-deficiency.md): Reduced ability to tell certain hues apart, most often red from green, which makes hue alone an unreliable way to carry meaning for roughly one man in twelve.
- [Conformance level](https://vocab.design/conformance-level.md): The A, AA, or AAA tier a WCAG success criterion sits in, and the tier a product claims, which is what people mean when they say a design is AA.
- [Consistent help](https://vocab.design/consistent-help.md): Keeping the same help route, a contact link, a chat launcher, a self-help pane, in the same relative place on every page so a stuck reader can find it again.
- [Consistent identification](https://vocab.design/consistent-identification.md): Calling the same function by the same name and icon everywhere in a product, so a reader who learned it once does not have to relearn it per screen.
- [Curb cut effect](https://vocab.design/curb-cut-effect.md): The pattern where something built for a disabled minority turns out to serve everyone, the way dropped kerbs serve prams and captions serve noisy rooms.
- [Current page indicator](https://vocab.design/current-page-indicator.md): The marking of which item in a navigation set is the one you are on, exposed with aria-current so it survives without the colour cue.
- [Decorative image](https://vocab.design/decorative-image.md): An image that carries no information and is given an empty alt attribute so assistive technology skips it entirely.
- [Dragging alternative](https://vocab.design/dragging-alternative.md): A second, non-dragging route to anything a drag can do, such as arrow keys or a move-to menu on a sortable list.
- [Error identification](https://vocab.design/error-identification.md): Naming the field that failed and saying what went wrong in text, rather than only outlining the input in red.
- [Escape gesture](https://vocab.design/escape-gesture.md): The screen reader equivalent of the Escape key, a two finger scrub that dismisses a sheet or steps back a level.
- [Expanded state](https://vocab.design/expanded-state.md): The open or closed state of a disclosure, exposed with aria-expanded on the control that owns it rather than on the panel it reveals.
- [Explore by touch](https://vocab.design/explore-by-touch.md): The touch screen reader mode where dragging a finger reads whatever is under it and activation takes a second, deliberate tap, so nothing fires by accident.
- [First rule of ARIA](https://vocab.design/first-rule-of-aria.md): The maxim that no ARIA is better than bad ARIA: if a native element does the job, use it rather than pinning a role onto a div and reimplementing the behaviour.
- [Flashing content](https://vocab.design/flashing-content.md): Content that flashes more than three times per second in a large enough area, restricted because it can trigger seizures.
- [Focus appearance](https://vocab.design/focus-appearance.md): The size and contrast a focus indicator must reach to count as visible: enough area around the control, enough change against both the control and its background.
- [Focus delegation](https://vocab.design/focus-delegation.md): A shadow root option that forwards focus from the host into the first focusable element inside it, so clicking the padding of a custom element does not leave focus nowhere.
- [Focus management](https://vocab.design/focus-management.md): Deliberately moving keyboard focus after a state change so the reader lands on the new content instead of at the top of the document.
- [Focus not obscured](https://vocab.design/focus-not-obscured.md): The requirement that a focused control is not completely hidden by sticky headers, footers, cookie bars, or chat widgets when it receives focus.
- [Focus order](https://vocab.design/focus-order.md): The sequence keyboard focus follows through a page, which should match reading order instead of source quirks or positive tabindex values.
- [Focus ring](https://vocab.design/focus-ring.md): The visible outline drawn around the element that currently holds keyboard focus, showing where the next keypress will land.
- [Focus trap](https://vocab.design/focus-trap.md): A constraint that keeps keyboard focus cycling inside one region until that region is dismissed.
- [Focus visible](https://vocab.design/focus-visible.md): A focus style shown only when focus arrived by keyboard or another non-pointer route, so a mouse click does not leave a ring behind.
- [Focusable disabled](https://vocab.design/focusable-disabled.md): A control styled as unavailable but left in the tab order with aria-disabled, so a reader can find it and learn why it is off.
- [Focusable scroll region](https://vocab.design/focusable-scroll-region.md): Giving a scrollable box its own tab stop so a keyboard user can scroll it, which matters whenever the content inside holds no focusable element of its own.
- [Functional need](https://vocab.design/functional-need.md): A statement of the gap between what a person can do and what a design demands, the WCAG 3 draft's way of naming a barrier without sorting people into disability categories.
- [Group label](https://vocab.design/group-label.md): The one name that covers a set of controls, a question above its radio buttons or a heading above an address block, so each field is heard in context.
- [Has popup](https://vocab.design/has-popup.md): A hint on a trigger that says something will open and what kind of thing it will be, a menu, a listbox, a dialog, before the reader commits to pressing it.
- [Header association](https://vocab.design/table-header-association.md): The markup that ties a data cell to its row and column headers, so a cell read on its own still says what it is.
- [Heading hierarchy](https://vocab.design/heading-hierarchy.md): The nested outline formed by heading levels, navigated directly by assistive technology and broken by skipping a level or picking a level for its size.
- [Hidden but focusable](https://vocab.design/hidden-but-focusable.md): An element hidden from assistive technology that is still in the tab sequence, so keyboard focus lands on something a screen reader refuses to describe.
- [Hoverable, dismissible, persistent](https://vocab.design/hoverable-dismissible-persistent.md): The three conditions content revealed on hover or focus must meet: reachable with the pointer, dismissible without moving focus, and not self-closing.
- [Images of text](https://vocab.design/images-of-text.md): Text baked into a raster image, which cannot be resized, restyled, selected, translated, or read by anything but the alt attribute someone remembered to write.
- [Increased contrast](https://vocab.design/prefers-contrast.md): A user preference for more contrast than a theme's default, honoured by strengthening borders, text, and state colours rather than by shifting hues.
- [Inert](https://vocab.design/inert.md): A state that removes a subtree from focus order, hit testing, and the accessibility tree at once, used to seal the background behind a dialog.
- [Initial focus](https://vocab.design/initial-focus.md): Where focus lands when a view, dialog, or page first appears, chosen deliberately rather than left on the body or dumped on the first close button.
- [Input purpose](https://vocab.design/input-purpose.md): Machine readable autocomplete tokens on personal fields, which let browsers autofill and let personalisation tools add familiar icons or wording.
- [Invalid state](https://vocab.design/invalid-state.md): The programmatic mark that a field's value failed validation, paired with a pointer to the message that explains it.
- [Inverted colors](https://vocab.design/inverted-colors.md): A whole-screen colour inversion applied by the OS, which flips a design nobody tested upside down and turns every shadow into a highlight.
- [Keyboard trap](https://vocab.design/keyboard-trap.md): A place keyboard focus can enter but not leave by keyboard alone, stranding anyone who is not using a pointer.
- [Label association](https://vocab.design/label-association.md): The programmatic link between a label and its field, made by for and id or by wrapping, which makes the label clickable and the field named.
- [Label in name](https://vocab.design/label-in-name.md): The rule that a control's accessible name must contain its visible label text, so speaking the visible words works in voice control.
- [Landmark](https://vocab.design/landmark.md): A named region role (banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo, search) that lets assistive technology jump between the major parts of a page.
- [Language attribute](https://vocab.design/language-attribute.md): The declared language of a document or a passage inside it, which picks the voice, the pronunciation rules, and the hyphenation a reader gets.
- [Large text threshold](https://vocab.design/large-text-threshold.md): The size at which text counts as large for contrast purposes (about 18pt, or 14pt when bold) and its required ratio drops from 4.5:1 to 3:1.
- [Line focus](https://vocab.design/line-focus.md): A reading aid that dims everything except one to five lines of text, so the eye has a single band to track and cannot skip or reread a line by accident.
- [Link purpose](https://vocab.design/link-purpose.md): Whether a link's own text says where it goes, the reason a list of read more and click here links fails when read out of context.
- [Live region](https://vocab.design/live-region.md): A container marked so assistive technology reads changes inside it without moving focus, used for messages that appear after an action.
- [Long description](https://vocab.design/long-description.md): An extended text alternative for a chart, diagram, or map, linked or referenced because a short alt string cannot carry the content.
- [Magic tap](https://vocab.design/magic-tap.md): A screen reader gesture that fires the one action a screen is most likely about, so the reader does not have to hunt for the control.
- [Mixed state checkbox](https://vocab.design/mixed-state-checkbox.md): A checkbox showing a third, indeterminate state when only some of the boxes it governs are checked.
- [Motion actuation](https://vocab.design/motion-actuation.md): Triggering a function by moving the device itself, such as shake to undo, which needs a plain control alternative and an off switch.
- [Name, role, value](https://vocab.design/name-role-value.md): The three things every control has to expose to assistive technology: what it is called, what kind of thing it is, and what state it is currently in.
- [Nested interactive](https://vocab.design/nested-interactive.md): A focusable control placed inside another control, such as a button inside a link or a checkbox inside a clickable row, which garbles the announcement and can leave the inner control unreachable.
- [Non-text contrast](https://vocab.design/non-text-contrast.md): The requirement that controls, focus indicators and meaningful graphics reach 3:1 against what is next to them, which is the rule that governs borders and icons.
- [Orientation lock](https://vocab.design/orientation-lock.md): Restricting a screen to portrait or landscape, which strands anyone whose device is fixed in a mount or a wheelchair arm in the orientation the design refused.
- [Owned element](https://vocab.design/owned-element.md): A child the accessibility tree is told to adopt from elsewhere in the DOM, used when the nesting a role requires is impossible in the markup.
- [Page title](https://vocab.design/page-title.md): The document title, the first thing a screen reader speaks and the only label a reader has when picking between tabs, windows, and history entries.
- [Pause, stop, hide](https://vocab.design/pause-stop-hide.md): A visible control for content that moves, blinks, scrolls, or updates on its own, so a reader can stop it before reading around it.
- [Placeholder as label](https://vocab.design/placeholder-as-label.md): The antipattern of using placeholder text as a field's only label, which vanishes on typing and usually fails both contrast and naming.
- [Plain language](https://vocab.design/plain-language.md): Writing interface copy at the reading level of the people using it, with short sentences, familiar words, and the point first, rather than at the level of the org chart.
- [Pointer cancellation](https://vocab.design/pointer-cancellation.md): Activating a control on pointer release rather than press, so someone who lands on the wrong target can slide off and abort.
- [Pointer gestures](https://vocab.design/pointer-gestures.md): Path based or multi finger gestures such as pinch, swipe, and drag along a track, which need a single pointer equivalent to stay operable.
- [Politeness level](https://vocab.design/politeness-level.md): The urgency setting on a live region: polite waits for a pause in speech, assertive interrupts whatever is being read.
- [Positive tabindex](https://vocab.design/positive-tabindex.md): Using tabindex values above zero to force an order, which yanks those elements to the front of the whole page sequence and is almost always a bug.
- [POUR](https://vocab.design/pour.md): The four principles WCAG is built on, perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust, used as a shorthand for sorting an accessibility problem into a bucket.
- [Presentation role](https://vocab.design/presentation-role.md): Stripping an element of its semantics while leaving it on screen, so a table used for layout or a list used for spacing stops being announced as one.
- [Presentational children](https://vocab.design/presentational-children.md): The rule that some roles flatten everything inside them into their own label, which is why an icon and a span inside a button are never announced separately.
- [Pronunciation](https://vocab.design/pronunciation.md): How a synthetic voice says a word, and the hints an author can give when the default reading turns a product name, a units string, or a homograph into nonsense.
- [Read aloud](https://vocab.design/read-aloud.md): Speaking a page's own prose with a synthetic voice, highlighting each word as it is spoken. A reading aid for people who can see the screen, not a screen reader.
- [Reader mode](https://vocab.design/reader-mode.md): A browser view that throws away your layout and rebuilds the article as plain text the reader can restyle, which is a verdict on how readable the original was.
- [Reading flow](https://vocab.design/reading-flow.md): A CSS property that repoints reading and tab order at the visual arrangement of a flex or grid container, instead of leaving both stuck in source order.
- [Reading order](https://vocab.design/reading-order.md): The order content is exposed in the DOM, which drives both speech output and tab order, and which visual reordering can silently contradict.
- [Reduced motion](https://vocab.design/prefers-reduced-motion.md): A user preference asking interfaces to cut non-essential animation, honoured by shortening, cross fading, or removing movement rather than by doing nothing.
- [Reduced transparency](https://vocab.design/reduced-transparency.md): A user preference asking for opaque surfaces instead of blur and translucency, honoured by swapping frosted layers for solid fills.
- [Redundant entry](https://vocab.design/redundant-entry.md): The rule against asking for the same information twice in one process, unless it is re-entered for a real reason such as confirmation.
- [Reflow](https://vocab.design/reflow.md): The requirement that content works in one column at 320 CSS pixels wide without two dimensional scrolling, which is 400 percent zoom on a desktop.
- [Required field indicator](https://vocab.design/required-field-indicator.md): How a form says a field cannot be left empty, in the label text, in the announced name, and not by an asterisk whose meaning is explained somewhere else.
- [Resize text](https://vocab.design/resize-text.md): Text must scale to at least 200 percent without loss of content or function, which rules out fixed pixel heights around wrapping copy.
- [Review cursor](https://vocab.design/review-cursor.md): A second cursor a screen reader user can move over the screen to read text without moving the system focus, so inspecting a region does not disturb the app.
- [Role description](https://vocab.design/role-description.md): An author supplied name for a widget's role, spoken in place of the stock role name, which overrides the platform wording and misleads easily.
- [Rotor](https://vocab.design/rotor.md): VoiceOver's dial for choosing what a swipe or flick moves between: headings, links, landmarks, form controls, or characters.
- [Route announcement](https://vocab.design/route-announcement.md): Telling assistive technology that a client side navigation happened, by moving focus to the new heading or posting the new title to a live region.
- [Screen curtain](https://vocab.design/screen-curtain.md): A screen reader mode that switches the display off entirely while navigation keeps working, used for privacy and by sighted testers checking an audio-only run.
- [Screen magnification](https://vocab.design/screen-magnification.md): Blowing part of the screen up many times over, so a reader sees a keyhole of the layout at a time and anything far from the action is effectively off screen.
- [Screen reader](https://vocab.design/screen-reader.md): Software that speaks or brailles the accessibility tree and supplies its own keyboard commands for moving through a page.
- [Semantic HTML](https://vocab.design/semantic-html.md): Reaching for the element that already means what you mean, so name, role, keyboard behaviour, and platform conventions arrive for free instead of being rebuilt.
- [Sensory characteristics](https://vocab.design/sensory-characteristics.md): Instructions that lean on shape, size, position, or sound alone, such as the round button on the right, which fail when those cues are not perceived.
- [Set size and position](https://vocab.design/set-size-and-position.md): Telling assistive technology how big a list really is and where an item sits in it, so a windowed or paginated list still announces "item 6 of 16".
- [Sign language interpretation](https://vocab.design/sign-language-interpretation.md): A signed track alongside video, presented as an inset or a companion stream, for readers whose first language is a sign language rather than the written caption text.
- [Situational disability](https://vocab.design/situational-disability.md): A barrier that comes from the moment rather than the body, one arm holding a baby, sunlight on a screen, a noisy train, and that makes the audience for access everyone.
- [Skip link](https://vocab.design/skip-link.md): A link at the very start of a page, revealed on focus, that jumps past repeated navigation to the main content.
- [Sonification](https://vocab.design/sonification.md): Turning data into sound, mapping a series to pitch or rhythm, so a chart can be heard as a shape rather than described one value at a time.
- [Sort state](https://vocab.design/sort-state.md): The announced direction of the one column a table is currently sorted by, carried on that column header alone rather than on every sortable header.
- [Spatial navigation](https://vocab.design/spatial-navigation.md): Moving focus by direction rather than by sequence, so arrow keys, a D-pad, or a TV remote jump to the nearest control up, down, left, or right.
- [Status message](https://vocab.design/status-message.md): A change in content that reports progress, result, or state and must be announced without taking focus, such as a count of search results.
- [Streaming announcement](https://vocab.design/streaming-announcement.md): How a screen reader is told about text that arrives token by token, holding the region quiet while it streams and speaking once when the answer is complete.
- [Switch access](https://vocab.design/switch-access.md): Operating a device with one or two switches, where a scanning cursor steps through targets in turn and a press selects the highlighted one.
- [Symbol support](https://vocab.design/symbol-support.md): Marking a control with a concept code so a reader who uses an augmentative symbol set sees their own familiar picture in place of your icon and wording.
- [Tab stop](https://vocab.design/tab-stop.md): One position in the tab sequence: a place the Tab key can reach, counted once even when the widget it belongs to holds many focusable parts.
- [Tabbable](https://vocab.design/tabbable.md): Reachable by the Tab key, as opposed to merely focusable: an element with tabindex of -1 can take focus from script but never from Tab.
- [Target spacing](https://vocab.design/target-spacing.md): The exception that lets an undersized control pass when no other target falls inside a 24 pixel circle centred on it, trading size for clearance.
- [Text spacing](https://vocab.design/text-spacing.md): The requirement that a reader can increase line height, letter spacing, word spacing, and paragraph spacing without any content being lost or clipped.
- [Timeout warning](https://vocab.design/timeout-warning.md): A warning before a session or form expires with a simple way to extend it, so a slower reader does not lose their work silently.
- [Touch target size](https://vocab.design/touch-target-size.md): The minimum area a control must offer a finger or imprecise pointer, measured on the activation region rather than the painted glyph.
- [Transcript](https://vocab.design/transcript.md): A full text version of time based media, readable without playing it and searchable by both people and machines.
- [Use of color](https://vocab.design/use-of-color.md): The rule that colour must never be the only carrier of meaning, so a red field also needs an icon, wording, or shape change.
- [Verbosity](https://vocab.design/verbosity.md): How much a screen reader says about each thing it reaches, a user setting that decides whether your carefully written description is heard at all.
- [Visually hidden](https://vocab.design/visually-hidden.md): Content removed from the visual layout but left in the accessibility tree, so screen readers announce what the design leaves unsaid.
- [Voice control](https://vocab.design/voice-control.md): Operating an interface by speaking control names or numbered overlays, which makes the visible wording of a control its address.
